title: Mendwell: Q4 2025 check-in
summary: Mendwell check-in: ARR at €1.97m (+16% QoQ) and Series B planned for Q4 2026. Main needs: deals with consultancies stalling at legal review.
body:
### Attendees
- Elin Aaltonen (Founder & CEO, Mendwell)
- {{user:i03}} (Principal, Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Regular check-in with Elin Aaltonen. We covered where the numbers are, sales motion and what shipped.

### Where the numbers are
- Run-rate revenue at €1.97m, +16% QoQ
  - 8 new logos in the quarter; biggest new contract €85k ACV
  - About 18% ahead of the board plan of €1.67m, mostly thanks to an early renewal with expansion
- Cash in the bank around €3.7m after the last tranche
  - Collections slightly slower; DSO around 53 days
  - No covenant questions from the bank this quarter
- 3,572 active patients across 43 clinics
  - 90-day adherence around 65%
- Net revenue retention around 116%
  - Expansion driven by new care pathways
  - 1 customer churned: a hospital pilot that ended without budget
- Net burn at €176k/month, runway until July 2027 (21 months)
  - Gross margin at 70%
  - Elin wants to keep the burn multiple under 1.3x
- Monthly revenue growth averaged 5% over the quarter
  - Best month was the last one, helped by a large expansion
- 43 customers with an average contract value of €46k
  - Top 10 customers are 55% of revenue

### Sales motion
- Deals with large consultancies tend to stall at legal review
  - Third time this year, most recently with Ashgrove Strategy Partners
  - Elin thinks they are pitching the wrong business case
- Weighted pipeline of €770k for Q1 2026, with 11 deals in contract negotiation
  - Largest opportunity: Dijkwacht Insurance at ~€170k; champion is Esmee van Leeuwen (Financial Controller)
  - Win rate 20% over the last two quarters
- Sales cycle averaging 205 days, roughly stable
  - Pilot sign-off by a second department add three to four weeks on larger deals
- Inbound is about 27% of new pipeline
  - Content and community are doing most of the work
  - Cold outbound converts best with hospital boards
- Competition: mostly up against hospital in-house solutions
  - Win when compliance depth matters; they lose on price
  - Lost two deals last quarter to a bundled offer
- Sales team: 4 AEs ramped and one SDR
  - Attainment around 58% for ramped reps
  - First sales manager starts in October
- ACV on new deals trending up to €60k
  - Larger deals bring longer pilots
- Product-led trials at 194 a month, 6% convert to paid
  - Time to first value is the main lever for SMB accounts

### What shipped
- Shipped remote onboarding for patients
  - Early adoption at 49% of active customers in the first month
  - Feedback positive overall; main request is reimbursement in Germany
- Released a patient app redesign
  - It took 4 weeks with three engineers
- Next priority: CE marking for the next device class
  - Aiming for end of Q1 2026
  - Clara thinks the date is realistic if scope stays fixed
- Spent ~24% of engineering time on reliability
  - Customer-facing incidents down from 7 to 4 per month
  - Clara wants to bring it down once the platform work lands
- Exploring AI assistance for the most repetitive workflows
  - Pricing for it undecided: add-on vs. included in the top tier
  - Early users report saving 8 hours a week
- Design-partner group met in September with six customers
  - Most requested: an API
  - Validated the next two roadmap items
- Engineering team at 8 people in four squads
  - Releases daily, cycle time down

### People & hiring
- Team at 35 people, aim to reach 46 by end of 2026
  - Regretted attrition low this year
- Will open a Site Reliability Engineer role in the next few weeks
  - Job description in draft; {{user:i03}} to review
- Salary bands due a refresh; option pool top-up needed before Q1 2026
  - Current pool has ~1.2% unallocated
- Recruiting largely via referrals
  - Referrals account for 44% of hires this year
  - Average time to hire around 43 days
- New-joiner onboarding still ad hoc; buddy system planned
  - Recent hires rate onboarding 7/10

### Capital plan
- Runway to July 2027; plan is to raise a Series B of around €18.8m starting in Q4 2026
  - Target metrics for the round: €3.54m ARR with NRR above 110%
- Targeting investors who know health tech and can help with US expansion
  - Tiago Demir (Dune & Delta Ventures) reached out after the last update
  - Wants to run a tight process: four weeks from first meetings to term sheet

### Partners
- Pilot discussions with Rivierland Hospital Group about a joint offering
  - Moving slowly: their budget cycle is the bottleneck
  - Potential value €170k in the first year if it works
- Partner-sourced pipeline at 9% of total
  - Want to double that by the end of Q1 2026
- Exploring an integration with Mossgrid (also Stroopwafel portfolio)
  - Intro made via {{user:i03}} to their founders
- Reseller partners: first one producing leads
  - Referral fee of 10–20% on first-year revenue
- Co-marketing planned for November with an accounting firm
  - Aiming for 100–200 registrations across their ICP

### Asks & opportunities
- Not an explicit ask: they lack a relationship with decision makers at consultancies like Ashgrove Strategy Partners; an insider view would help.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:i03}}: check who knows the energy practice at Ashgrove Strategy Partners (by 30 Oct)
- [ ] Elin: share the draft board deck (by 24 Oct)
- [ ] {{user:i03}}: share these notes with the deal team (by 25 Oct)

title: Candidate chat: Roos Bosman
summary: Intro chat with Roos Bosman (Director of Engineering, Wavelength Audio).
body:
### Attendees
- Roos Bosman (Director of Engineering, Wavelength Audio)
- {{user:p11}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Exploratory chat with Roos Bosman, who reached out through our website. Exploring next steps and possible roles in the portfolio. We wanted to get a feel for their profile before sharing it with founders.

### Experience
- Currently Director of Engineering at Wavelength Audio (2023–present)
  - Owned reliability and on-call; cut incident volume by half.
  - Strongest stories are about hiring engineers and engineering leadership
- Before that Senior Software Engineer at Cloudmere (2016–2021)
  - Led the platform team through a migration from a monolith to services.
- Before that Software Engineer at Dijkwacht Insurance (2013–2016)
  - Hands-on role, reporting to the founders
- Based in Amsterdam, Netherlands; prefers remote-first teams
  - Travel fine two or three days a week
- Has a degree in law in the Netherlands, then consulting
  - Fluent in English, Dutch and German
- Career pattern: steady progression
  - Moved for the team, rather than for title
  - No break in the CV, explained by a sabbatical
- Outside work: mentors at an accelerator
  - Good indicator of community standing

### Fit with portfolio roles
- Nothing live in the portfolio that fits right now
  - Keep warm for the next wave of Series A hiring
- Coming up: Nordlicht Analytics is planning to open a Integrations Engineer role soon
  - Worth mention Roos to Nordlicht Analytics before the role goes live
- Upcoming: Solenne Storage expects to open a Senior Data Engineer role in the coming months
  - Good to flag Roos to Solenne Storage before the role goes live
- Outside the portfolio, Roos has interest from two Series B companies
  - So we should move quickly if a founder is interested

### Comp & availability
- Current base roughly €103k; looking for €118k–€131k plus equity
  - Open to more equity for a lower base if the story is strong
- Notice period is one months
  - Earliest start around early Q1 2026
- Talking to 4 other companies
  - Would like to make a decision before the end of the quarter
- Benefits that matter: flexible hours
  - Not a dealbreaker, but it came up twice
- Open to a fractional start before committing
  - Has done this before at their last role and it worked well
- Visa not needed; already living in the Netherlands
  - Their family situation supports a start in Q1 2026
- Counter-offer risk real: they have been promoted recently
  - Worth keeping the process tight if a company is interested

### How they work
- Has managed teams of 19 people
  - Describes their style as high-context and hands-off
- Strongest example: rebuilt an underperforming team in six months
  - Numbers held up when we probed
- Hardest moment: a layoff round
  - Honest about what they would do differently
- Decision-making: data first, then gut
  - Gave an example from a vendor choice
- On feedback: asks for it weekly
  - Matches what their reference told us
- Hiring track record: promoted three people internally
  - Uses structured interviews

### Strengths & watch-outs
- Clear strengths: engineering leadership plus consumer tech
  - Gave concrete examples with numbers, which is rare
- Watch-out: has not managed managers yet
  - Worth probing in references
- Communication crisp; would suit a fast-moving team
  - Should test how they handle ambiguity in a working session
- Team fit: good at bringing structure to chaos
  - Would complement a visionary founder
- Self-awareness good: was clear about what they still need to learn unprompted
  - Wants a founder who will coach them on strategy
- Overall: good, not yet exceptional
  - Will share the profile with one or two founders before a wider share
  - Our rating: 4 out of 5 on the talent scorecard
- Main risk for a hiring manager: may want to move faster to management than the role allows
  - Way to handle it: discuss the growth path openly

### Questions they asked
- Asked several questions about runway at the portfolio companies
  - Good sign they have been burned before
- Wanted to know how Stroopwafel supports portfolio hires in the first 90 days
  - Pointed them to the operator community run by {{user:p11}}
- Asked about equity norms at this stage in the Netherlands
  - Gave rough ranges and the new tax treatment of options
- Wanted to know where the strongest teams are among our companies
  - Kept it general; offered specific intros once there is a concrete role
- Wanted to know what the hardest part of the role would be
  - Sharp question, showing interest in the team not just perks

### Asks & opportunities
- Roos asked for intros to companies hiring in hiring engineers.
- Opportunity: Roos could refer two or three strong people from their network.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:p11}}: add to the talent pool with tags (by 25 Oct)
- [ ] Roos: send an updated CV (by 24 Oct)
- [ ] {{user:p11}}: schedule the next check-in (by 22 Oct)

title: Catch-up with Davide Bianchi (Kettlebridge)

body:
### Attendees
- Davide Bianchi (CEO & Co-founder, Kettlebridge)
- {{user:i03}} (Principal, Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
1:1 catch-up with Davide Bianchi over lunch near their office. Davide wanted to talk through pipeline & sales, fundraising plans and founder check-in.

### Pipeline & sales
- Founder-led sales is hitting its limit; enterprise deals keep getting stuck after the first demo
  - Davide raised it but has no owner for it yet
- Weighted pipeline of €440k for Q1 2026, and 6 deals in late stage
  - Largest opportunity: Cloudmere at ~€264k; champion is Wei Seidel (Senior Partner Manager)
  - Win rate 36% over the last two quarters
- Sales cycle averaging 110 days, roughly stable
  - Pilot sign-off by a second department add three to four weeks on larger deals
- Inbound is roughly 50% of new pipeline
  - Founder posts and talks still drive most of it
  - Cold outbound converts best with heads of legal
- Competition: mostly up against legacy on-premise vendors
  - Win when local support matters; lose on price
  - Dropped two deals this quarter on price alone

### Fundraising plans
- Runway until November 2027; planning to raise a Series B of around €20.4m starting in Q1 2027
  - Target metrics for the round: €1.8m ARR with NRR above 110%
- Targeting investors who know B2B SaaS and have led rounds at this stage before
  - Irene Campos (Oakmeadow Partners) reached out after the last update
  - Prefers to run a tight process: four weeks from first meetings to term sheet
- Stroopwafel will likely consider an internal extension if the market is slow
  - {{user:i03}} to discuss at the next partner meeting
- Considering a revenue-based facility to extend runway by six months
  - Two lenders are in conversation
- Expectations on valuation ambitious: 19x ARR
  - {{user:i03}} suggested a clean structure matters more than headline valuation

### Founder check-in
- Davide is tired but upbeat
  - Spending ~48% of their week on hiring
  - Wants to hand over day-to-day sales by Q1 2026
- Co-founder dynamics good; clear ownership between Davide and Merel
  - Fortnightly founder 1:1 working well
- Open to a CEO peer group
  - {{user:i03}} to share a shortlist
- Leadership team still uneven: strongest in product, weakest in people
  - Upcoming senior hire probably in one of the thin areas
- Asked for advice on letting go of an early employee
  - {{user:i03}} shared a template from another portfolio company

### Team & hiring
- Team at 20 people, aim to reach 26 by end of 2026
  - Attrition 0 people in the last six months
- Will open a Account Executive role in the next few weeks
  - Job description being drafted; {{user:i03}} to review
- Comp bands due a refresh; ESOP refresh needed before Q1 2026
  - Current pool has ~2.3% unallocated
- Recruiting largely in-house
  - Referrals account for 37% of hires this year
  - Time to hire about 42 days
- Onboarding still ad hoc; 30-60-90 plans introduced
  - Recent hires scored onboarding 6/10, up from last quarter

### Roadmap
- Shipped a mobile app for frontline users
  - Adoption at 68% of active customers after 2 weeks
  - Feedback positive overall; main request is an enterprise tier
- Also shipped AI-assisted drafting
  - Took 7 weeks with three engineers
- Next up: German and French localisation
  - Targeting Q1 2026
  - Depends on the senior backend hire landing
- Spending ~28% of engineering time on paying down technical debt
  - Incidents down from 10 to 2 per month
  - Merel wants to keep that ratio through Q1 2026
- Exploring AI assistance for the most repetitive workflows
  - Pricing for it undecided: add-on vs. included in the top tier
  - Early users report saving roughly 3 hours a week

### Partners
- In talks with Ashgrove Strategy Partners about a paid pilot
  - Moving slowly: their budget cycle is the bottleneck
  - Could be worth €399k in the first year if it works
- Partner-sourced pipeline now 28% of total
  - Want to double that by the end of Q1 2026
- Exploring an integration with Mossgrid (also Stroopwafel portfolio)
  - Intro made via {{user:i03}} to their founders
- Reseller partners: first one producing leads
  - Revenue share of 15% in year one
- Joint webinar planned for November with an industry association
  - Aiming for a few hundred registrations across target accounts

### Asks & opportunities
- Intros to operations directors in the US for the next sales push.
- No explicit ask: would benefit from a sales leader who has built a first enterprise team.
- Opportunity: Kettlebridge is happy to share learnings with other portfolio founders on pricing.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:i03}}: ask around the portfolio for operations directors in the US (by 28 Oct)
- [ ] {{user:i03}}: suggest one or two advisor options (sales) (by end of month)
- [ ] Davide: send the updated KPI sheet (by 3 Nov)

Exploratory chat with Elin Halvorsen, referred by a portfolio founder. Open to next steps and possible roles in the portfolio. Goal was to understand what they want next and where they could fit.

### Profile

### Asks & opportunities

title: Meeting with Ravelpay
summary: Meeting with Ravelpay about their priorities and how they run pilots with startups.
body:
### Attendees
- Paweł Marin (Head of Partnerships, Ravelpay)
- {{user:p08}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Follow-up meeting with Paweł Marin from Ravelpay about working with portfolio companies. They asked for the meeting after seeing our portfolio update.

### What they care about
- Number one priority: platform and marketplace merchants
  - Programme budget of roughly €1.1m for 2026
  - Board-level attention still being secured
- Another priority: faster payouts
  - Budget of roughly €2.7m this year
  - Executive attention in place
- Another priority: reducing merchant churn
  - Programme budget of roughly €1.2m for 2026
  - Executive attention still being secured
- Board pressure on growth in new segments for 2026
  - Startups positioned as a way to test ideas cheaply
- Targets tied to the programme have been set at board level
  - Progress checked quarterly by the executive committee
- The leadership team changed last year, bringing a new digital lead who is pushing for speed
  - Window to get in early while priorities are being set

### Portfolio fit
- Fennel Payroll: could help with merchant partnerships
  - Offers payroll and contractor payments; they'd want a sponsor in the business
- Quaycredit: relevant for the platform and marketplace team
  - Builds revenue-based financing; they'd want a sponsor in the business
- Ledgerbloom: could help with the platform and marketplace team
  - Offers accounts-payable automation; worth a first call
- Also interested in workforce planning even if outside the core brief
  - Small budget for now, but could run a test in Q1 2026
- Want a small number of well-prepared intros over a long list
  - Every intro should come with a one-pager and a clear use case
- Separately requested a list of startups in energy management
  - Will scan the portfolio and come back within two weeks

### Their organisation
- Paweł sits in the COO's office
  - Mandate: can open doors but cannot sign
- Suggested we also speak to Eleanor Brennan (Head of Product)
  - Close to the operational problem for this area
- Recent reorganisation shifted partnerships under the CFO
  - A lot of uncertainty about ownership for 2026
- Influence sits with central functions rather than the startup team
  - Best path: start with one country
- The IT team has a strong say on any integration
  - Worth involve them early

### How decisions get made
- Pilot budget for 2026 roughly €1.7m
  - BUs must co-fund anything beyond a pilot
- Decision makers sits with the BU director for anything above €100k
  - Steering committee convenes monthly
- Ideal timing for new proposals: during the autumn planning round
  - Late proposals almost never get funded
- Invoicing: 90 days by default; faster terms negotiable for small vendors
  - Worth flag early for smaller companies
- Multi-year contracts need CFO approval over €500k
  - Small pilots may be signed locally

### What has worked before
- Have run 12 startup pilots in the last two years
  - Only 3 became contracts
  - Successful ones had a business owner from day one
- Best collaboration: an analytics vendor that replaced an incumbent
  - Needed twelve months from pilot to full contract
- Failed pilots mostly stalled at the budget round
  - The team has started to pre-approve vendor paperwork
- Buying from startups now a formal programme with a small team
  - Team sits under IT

### Concerns
- Concern about startup longevity for critical processes
  - Answer: a Stroopwafel intro to the founders
- Previous startup collaborations: 7 pilots in two years, only one scaled
  - Why: no business owner after the pilot
- Their legal team insists on a full security questionnaire even for pilots
  - Template is fairly one-sided on IP; expect three rounds of comments
- Concerned about integration with legacy systems during a rollout
  - Asked for startups that bring implementation support
- Brand risk with customer-facing pilots
  - Want back-office use cases to start with

### Asks & opportunities
- Ravelpay wants a shortlist of startups for their 2026 plan.
- Paweł asked for a contact at a peer fund.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:p08}}: send a short intro note on Fennel Payroll (by 11 Dec)
- [ ] {{user:p08}}: send a short intro note on Quaycredit (by next week)
- [ ] Paweł: share the pilot criteria document (by 10 Dec)

### Relevant portfolio companies
- Fennel Payroll: relevant for risk and underwriting
  - Offers payroll and contractor payments; worth a first call
- Driftmark: relevant for merchant partnerships
  - Offers embedded insurance APIs; worth a first call
- Sluisline: relevant for merchant partnerships
  - Builds KYB and compliance automation; worth a first call

- Want one or two well-prepared intros over a long list
  - Every intro should come with a short case and a named use case
- Separately requested ideas for startups in workforce scheduling
  - To check the portfolio and revert by 16 Dec

### How they work with startups
- Pilots need a business sponsor and a multi-week security review
  - Paid pilots capped at roughly €80k
- Vendor onboarding via central procurement takes 14 weeks
  - Tip: start onboarding in parallel with the pilot
- Budget cycle closes in October; new initiatives must be in the plan by then
  - Late proposals need special approval
- Innovation team is two people and acts as a door-opener to the business units
  - Good entry point, but business units own the budgets
- Success measured on NPS after 16 weeks
  - Metrics set before the pilot starts with the sponsor
- IT security checklist has ~200 questions; SOC 2 helps a lot
  - Data must stay in the EU
- Contracting uses a framework agreement; liability caps take the longest
  - Tip: flag deviations early
- References are essential: they ask for two Dutch references ahead of any pilot
  - Our companies with strong local references stand out

### Previous startup collaborations
- Ran 5 startup pilots in the last two years
  - Only 3 became production deployments
  - The ones that worked had a business owner from day one
- Most successful partnership: a scheduling tool now used across the company
  - Took nine months from pilot to full contract
- Stalled projects mostly died at the budget round
  - They has started to involve procurement earlier
- Venture clienting is a formal programme with a small team
  - Programme sits under the COO

- Kenji reports into the COO's office
  - Influence: owns a small pilot budget
- Suggested we also speak to Bram Vermeulen (Partnerships Lead)
  - Close to the operational problem for this area
- Recent reorganisation shifted partnerships under the COO
  - A lot of uncertainty about budgets for 2026
- Influence lies with business units rather than the startup team
  - Best path: land a small paid pilot
- The CTO office holds a veto on any integration
  - Good idea to involve them before the pilot

- Innovation budget for 2026 about €2m, not yet approved
  - Business units must co-fund pilots
- Decision makers sits with the BU director for anything above €100k
  - The committee meets monthly
- Best timing for new pilots: during the autumn planning round
  - Late proposals almost never make it into the plan
- Invoicing: 60 days by default; shorter terms possible for startups
  - Important to flag early for smaller companies
- Longer commitments require CFO approval above €250k
  - Pilots may be approved by the BU director

### Asks & opportunities
- Ravelpay wants a shortlist of startups for their 2026 plan.
- Kenji asked for a benchmark of how other corporates run pilots.

### Next steps

- [ ] {{user:p16}}: send a short intro note on Driftmark (by next week)
- [ ] Kenji: share the pilot criteria document (by 19 Dec)

body:
### Attendees

- Franziska Kovač (Director of Engineering, Havenlink Logistics)
- {{user:p08}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)
- {{user:p10}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Intro meeting with Julian Hartmann and Franziska Kovač from Havenlink Logistics about working with portfolio companies. Follow-up from an earlier call with their innovation team.

### What they care about
- Number one priority: warehouse automation
  - Budget of roughly €2.4m for 2026
  - Executive attention still being secured
- Another priority: visibility for shippers
  - Programme budget of roughly €2.8m for 2026
  - Board-level attention in place
- Also: decarbonising road freight
  - Budget around €2.6m this year
  - Executive sponsor still being secured
- Executive focus on growth in new segments for 2026
  - Startups seen as a way to test ideas cheaply
- KPIs linked to the programme have been published internally
  - Status checked quarterly by the board
- Leadership was reshuffled last year, with a new digital lead keen on being pushing for speed
  - Window for new partners before budgets are locked

### Portfolio fit
- Mossgrid: could help with warehouse operations
  - Builds EV fleet charging orchestration; worth a first call
- Tenderloop: could help with warehouse operations
  - Offers procurement intake and supplier onboarding; worth a first call
- Carbonwick: could help with freight procurement
  - Offers carbon accounting; they'd want a sponsor in the business
- Open to hearing about AI tools for internal teams as a second track
  - Small budget yet, but could run a test in Q1 2026
- Prefer a small number of well-prepared intros over a long list
  - Every intro should come with a short case and a clear use case
- Also asked for ideas for startups in workforce scheduling
  - Will scan the wider network and revert within two weeks

### Budget and decision-making
- Innovation budget for 2026 roughly €800k, not yet approved
  - BUs must co-fund anything beyond a pilot
- Decision makers needs a steering committee for anything above €100k
  - The committee meets monthly
- Ideal timing for new pilots: in the first quarter
  - Last-minute proposals rarely make it into the plan
- Invoicing: 60 days standard; shorter terms negotiable for small vendors
  - Worth flag early for smaller companies
- Multi-year commitments need board approval over €250k
  - Pilots may be approved locally

### Risks they raised
- Worry about vendor concentration for critical processes
  - Mitigation: escrow and step-in rights
- Past startup collaborations: 7 pilots in two years, only one scaled
  - Why: budget not planned
- Their legal team insists on a full security questionnaire even for pilots
  - Their template is heavy on IP; plan for three rounds of comments
- Concerned about integration with legacy systems during a rollout
  - Asked for startups that bring implementation support
- Reputation risk with consumer-facing pilots
  - Prefer internal use cases first

### Who's who
- Julian sits in the strategy team
  - Influence: owns a small pilot budget
- Recommended Marloes Veldhuis (Head of Operations)
  - Owns the operational problem for the pilots we discussed
- Last reorganisation moved innovation under a new Chief Digital Officer
  - A lot of uncertainty about ownership for 2026
- Influence sits with central functions more than the innovation team
  - Best path: land a small paid pilot
- Their CTO office holds a veto on new vendors
  - Good idea to involve them before the pilot

### Previous startup collaborations
- Ran 12 startup pilots in the last two years, mostly in customer service
  - Just 3 turned into contracts
  - The ones that worked had a business owner from day one
- Most successful partnership: an analytics vendor that replaced an incumbent
  - Took twelve months from pilot to full contract
- Stalled pilots usually died at IT security
  - The team has started to involve procurement earlier
- Buying from startups is a formal programme with one dedicated person
  - Programme reports to strategy

### Asks & opportunities
- Havenlink Logistics wants a shortlist of startups for their 2026 plan.
- Julian asked for a contact at a peer fund.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:p08}}: send a short intro note on Mossgrid (by 25 Dec)
- [ ] {{user:p08}}: send a short intro note on Tenderloop (by next week)
- [ ] Julian: share the pilot criteria document (by 25 Dec)

### Context
Intro with Wouter Timmerman from Brightmoor Ventures to share deal flow. First proper meeting after a few emails.

### Fund overview
- Brightmoor Ventures deploying Fund II (€220m), first close in 2025
  - A seed fund focused on fintech and vertical software in the DACH region.

- Current portfolio of 15 companies, mostly in Benelux
  - Recent investments are a payments startup at seed
- Their LPs: a corporate anchor plus private investors
  - Fund raising expected in about two years
- Fund timeline: investment period runs to 2027 plus two years of follow-ons
  - Pace on track because of market conditions

### Deal flow from our side
- Tallyhaven (Series A, fintech): might raise in early 2027
  - Builds spend management and corporate cards; they asked for the deck
- Tenderloop (seed, B2B SaaS): planning a raise in early 2027
  - Builds procurement intake and supplier onboarding; they'd like the deck

- Open to sharing deal flow in shared focus areas

### Thesis & focus
- Focus areas: fintech and B2B SaaS

- Staying away from consumer for now
  - Lesson from a write-off: be careful with capital-heavy models
- Their read on the market: seed valuations back to 2019 levels outside AI
  - Their LPs pushing for distributions more than ever

  - Happy to go higher for category leaders
- Due diligence style: data-room driven

### Market view

### Attendees
- Lars Wijnands (Head of Sales, Medilane)
- {{user:p04}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
First conversation with Lars Wijnands, whom we met at a community event. Exploring next steps and possible roles in the portfolio. Goal was to understand what they want next and where they could fit.

### Career so far
- Currently Head of Sales at Medilane (2019–present)
  - Built the outbound motion and the SDR team.
  - Best examples are about mid-market sales and pipeline building
- Earlier Head of Sales at Havenlink Logistics (2016–2018)
  - Hands-on role, reporting to the founders
- Before that Head of Sales at Tellerbird (2013–2016)
  - Broad remit, reporting to the founders
- Based in the Netherlands, happy to commute to Amsterdam three days a week
  - Commute fine for team days
- Studied econometrics abroad, then a graduate programme
  - Fluent in Dutch and English
- Pattern: roughly three years per role
  - Moved for scope, not just for title
  - One gap in the CV, explained by a sabbatical
- Side projects: angel invests small tickets
  - Useful indicator of network

### Possible roles
- Nothing live in the portfolio that fits right now
  - Worth keeping warm for the next wave of Series A hiring
- Upcoming: Annotaire is planning to open a Enterprise Account Executive role soon
  - Good to flag Lars to Annotaire early
- Coming up: Tenderloop is planning to open a Solutions Engineer role soon
  - Worth mention Lars to Tenderloop early
- Beyond our companies, Lars has interest from a US company opening in Amsterdam
  - So we need to move fast if someone is interested

### What's next
- Looking for a move into more ownership at a growth-stage company
  - Preferred sectors: mid-market sales, pipeline building and outbound
  - Wants founders who listen more than title
- Motivation for moving: growth has stalled where they are
  - Not in a hurry, but has started a few processes
- Team size: small and senior
  - Has not hired a team from zero before
  - Prefers player-coach roles to pure management
- Where: Amsterdam or remote within CET
  - Travel fine up to a week a month
- Red flags for them: founders who micromanage
  - Asked to see runway and burn before an offer
- Stage preference: post-product-market fit, ideally B2B
  - Has seen the 20-to-100 transition before and liked it
  - Not keen on consumer businesses
- Ideal start: fixing one urgent problem
  - Expects explicit goals from the CEO up front
- Industries they would rather avoid: gambling
  - Cares a lot about impact beyond the role
- Already has a view on which of our companies look interesting
  - Named a couple of companies from our website

### What they wanted to know
- Asked a lot about how decisions get made at the portfolio companies
  - Signals they think like an owner
- Wanted to know how Stroopwafel supports portfolio hires in the first 90 days
  - Pointed them to the operator community run by {{user:p04}}
- Asked about equity norms at this stage in the Netherlands
  - Shared rough ranges and the new tax treatment of options
- Asked where the strongest teams are among our companies
  - Kept it general; suggested to set up calls once there is a concrete role
- Asked who they would report to
  - Sharp question, showing interest in impact not just perks

### Timing
- Current base roughly €106k; looking for €118k–€131k plus equity
  - Equity matters if the story is strong
- Notice period of three months
  - Could start in early Q2 2026
- In process with 1 other companies, one at offer stage
  - Wants to make a decision within six weeks
- Benefits that matter: flexible hours
  - Not a dealbreaker, but clearly important to them
- Would consider a short contract or trial project to test the fit
  - Has done this before at their last role with good results
- Relocation not an issue; currently living in the Netherlands
  - Their family situation supports a start in early 2027
- Risk of a counter-offer real: they have been promoted recently
  - Worth keeping the process tight if a company is interested

### Assessment
- Strengths: outbound and pipeline building
  - Gave concrete examples with numbers
- Watch-outs: has not managed managers yet
  - Worth probing in references
- Communication warm, a bit long-winded; should do well with technical founders
  - Should test how they handle pushback in a case
- Culture add: good at bringing structure to chaos
  - Could balance a visionary founder
- Self-awareness strong: was clear about their gaps without prompting
  - Wants a manager who will stretch them on strategy
- Overall view: good, not yet exceptional
  - Would introduce them to one or two founders before a wider share
  - Our rating: 3.5 out of 5 on the talent scorecard
- Risk for a hiring manager: may want to move faster to management than the role allows
  - Mitigation: be explicit about scope

### Asks & opportunities
- Lars asked for intros to founders hiring in mid-market sales.
- Opportunity: Lars could refer a few strong people from their network.

- [ ] Lars: send an updated CV (by 18 Jan)
- [ ] {{user:p04}}: log the follow-ups in the CRM (by 16 Jan)

  - Third time this year, most recently with Dijkwacht Insurance
  - Katarzyna thinks they are pitching the wrong business case
- Weighted pipeline of €2.31m for Q2 2026, with 10 deals in contract negotiation
  - Biggest opportunity: Dijkwacht Insurance at ~€118k; champion is Sofía Mehta (Head of Partnerships)
  - Win rate 30% over the last two quarters
- Sales cycle currently 66 days
  - Data-protection questionnaires add three to four weeks on larger deals
- Inbound now roughly 25% of new pipeline
  - Content and community are doing most of the work
  - Outbound works best with treasury managers
- Competition: seeing a lot more of spreadsheets plus an outsourced bookkeeper
  - They win when integration depth matters; lose on price
  - Lost one deal last quarter to a bundled offer
- Sales team: 5 AEs in seat and 3 SDRs
  - Quota attainment at 75% across the team
  - New sales manager starts in January
- ACV on new deals up to €19k
  - Bigger deals come with more stakeholders
- Product-led signups around 281 a month, 10% convert to paid
  - Time to first value is the main lever for SMB accounts

### Next round
- Runway until April 2027; planning to raise a Series C of around €35.1m in Q3 2026
  - Target metrics for the round: €10.1m ARR with growth above 8% QoQ
- Targeting investors who know fintech
  - Léa Virtanen (Molenwiek Capital) already asked for the deck
  - Prefers to run a tight process: six weeks from first meetings to term sheet
- Stroopwafel will likely take its pro-rata
  - {{user:i01}} to discuss with the partnership

  - Two lenders are in conversation
- Valuation expectations ambitious: a step up of ~2x on the last round
  - {{user:i01}} suggested anchoring on growth quality instead

  - Target is to have it complete well before the first meetings

### International expansion
- Belgium is the priority market, a country lead planned for Q2 2026
  - 18% of pipeline already comes from Belgium
  - Localisation in progress
- The Nordics on hold until Belgium proves out
  - Inbound interest from there served from Amsterdam in the meantime
- Considering whether to enter through partners first
  - Katarzyna leans towards partners; {{user:i01}} suggested testing both
- Support in German needed within six months
  - Plan: hire locally

### What shipped
- Shipped the new onboarding flow that cut KYB time to under a day
  - Adoption at 65% of active customers after 6 weeks
  - Feedback mostly positive; main request is open-banking data in forecasts
- Released the accounting-software sync rewrite ahead of schedule
  - Took 5 weeks with two engineers
- Next big bet: self-serve onboarding for the smallest customers
  - Aiming for end of Q2 2026
  - Depends on the senior backend hire landing
- Spending ~35% of engineering time on reliability
  - Customer-facing incidents down from 8 to 1 per month
  - Daan wants to protect that time even when sales asks for features
- Exploring AI assistance for data entry and categorisation
  - Plan is to include it for free until usage is proven
  - Early users report saving 4 hours a week
- Customer advisory board ran in December with five customers
  - Most requested: deeper integrations
  - Surfaced a reporting gap the team had underestimated

### Founder check-in
- Katarzyna sounds energised
  - Spending ~32% of the week on fundraising prep
  - Wants to delegate operations by Q2 2026
- Co-founder dynamics in a better place; clear ownership between Katarzyna and Daan
  - Weekly founder 1:1 working well
- Considering an executive coach
  - {{user:p05}} to share a shortlist
- Leadership team still uneven: most effective in sales, thinnest in finance
  - Upcoming leadership hire likely in that area
- Asked for advice on how to run a leadership offsite
  - {{user:i01}} shared how two other founders approached it
- Taking a week off in February; the leadership team is ready to cover
  - {{user:i01}} encouraged it

### Asks & opportunities
- Intros to treasury managers in France as potential design partners.
- Implied: they lack a relationship with decision makers at insurers like Dijkwacht Insurance; an insider view would help.
- Looking for a sales leader who has built a first enterprise team for a few hours a month.

title: Haringvliet Partners: intro call
summary: Met Haringvliet Partners to compare notes and share deal flow; shared Klusjesclub, Carbonwick and Ateliermarkt as potential deals.
body:
### Attendees
- Teun Campos (Associate, Haringvliet Partners)
- Arjun Haddad (Partner, Haringvliet Partners)
- {{user:i04}} (Principal, Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Intro with Teun Campos and Arjun Haddad from Haringvliet Partners to explore co-investment opportunities. Second conversation this year.

### About the fund
- Haringvliet Partners is investing from Fund II (€85m), final close in 2023
  - A Dutch climate and circular-economy fund writing first institutional cheques.
  - About 74% deployed so far; aiming for 14 new investments a year
- Initial cheques of €1.02m–€3.4m, reserves of about 1.5x for follow-ons
  - Like to co-lead and take a board seat
- Team of 6 partners and a small investment team
  - Partners cover one or two sectors; investment decisions by consensus
- Current portfolio of 40 companies, largely in the UK and DACH
  - Latest investments include a grid-software company at Series A
- Their LPs: mostly family offices and a fund-of-funds
  - Fund raising planned in 2027
- Fund life: investment period runs to 2027 with two years of follow-ons
  - Deployment pace on track given market conditions

### Portfolio companies to share
- Klusjesclub (Series A, marketplaces): might raise in early 2027
  - Builds a marketplace for vetted local tradespeople; they'd like a first call
- Carbonwick (seed, climate tech): might raise in the next six months
  - Makes carbon accounting; they asked for the deck
- Ateliermarkt (seed, marketplaces): might raise in the next six months
  - Builds a booking marketplace for creative studios; they asked for a first call

### Relationship
- Keen on sharing deal flow where we overlap
  - Would like a quarterly call between the partnerships
- Process: partner meeting weekly, term sheet within four to six weeks of first meeting
  - Prefer warm intros via co-investors
- Value-add: talent network and an executive search partner
  - Founders rate it highly, especially for first US hires
- Reference calls: two founders recommend the partner in the room
  - Good to cross-check with our founders who know them
- Board style: hands-off between meetings
  - Founders say they are supportive in hard moments
- Usual co-investors: mostly UK and German funds
  - Open to meeting more Benelux partners

### Market notes
- Seeing about a third more Series A decks than last year, largely AI-related
  - Quality lower than the volume suggests
- Liquidity still slow: small trade sales remain the main route
  - They expect a few IPO windows in 2027
- Valuations stable outside AI
  - Boards pushing capital efficiency over growth at all costs
- Co-investment appetite strong for Benelux deals with a clear path to €10m ARR
  - Particularly interested in fintech follow-ons
- AI-native companies taking a large share of new capital
  - Other founders need clear unit economics to raise
- Secondary market growing; early employees selling small amounts in later rounds
  - Mixed views on whether it helps retention

### How we could collaborate
- Will share pipeline every quarter in overlapping sectors
  - Start with: a short list of companies we are both tracking
- Talked about co-hosting a CFO roundtable together
  - {{user:i04}} to check the calendar for Q2 2026
- Interested in meeting corporate venture teams we know
  - Reciprocal, they offered their talent network
- Hiring collaboration: agreed to share candidates for senior roles
  - {{user:i04}} to connect with their talent lead
- Discussed a light rule: tell each other early when evaluating the same company
  - Avoids unnecessary competition on overlapping deals

### Recent activity
- Haringvliet Partners made 8 new investments in the last twelve months
  - Mainly seed rounds of €2.6m–€5.8m
  - One follow-on syndicated with German funds
- Strongest companies sit in payments
  - Two up-rounds in the past year; no write-offs so far
- Platform is a bigger part of the pitch: finance programmes
  - Interested in joint workshops with {{user:i04}}
- Reserves tighter than they would like for the current fund
  - May need co-investors for larger rounds
- Exits in the previous fund: two small acquisitions
  - DPI below where LPs want it
- Notable company just raised a large round with a London growth fund
  - Positive signal for follow-on demand more broadly

### Asks & opportunities
- Haringvliet Partners asked to see more climate tech and marketplaces deal flow from us.
- Opportunity: swap notes on two companies we are both tracking.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:i04}}: send the Klusjesclub one-pager (by 5 Feb)
- [ ] {{user:i04}}: send the Carbonwick one-pager (by 5 Feb)
- [ ] {{user:i04}}: send the Ateliermarkt one-pager (by next week)
- [ ] Teun: share their current portfolio list (by 5 Feb)

### Attendees
- Lukas Albrecht (Senior Account Executive, Pebblepath)
- {{user:p11}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)
- {{user:i02}} (General Partner, Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Exploratory chat with Lukas Albrecht, who reached out through our website. Exploring next steps and possible roles in the portfolio. We wanted to get a feel for their profile before sharing it with founders.

### Experience
- Currently Senior Account Executive at Pebblepath (2026–present)
  - Broad remit, reporting to the founders
  - Strongest stories are about mid-market sales and B2B sales
- Earlier Senior Account Executive at Carrotcake Studio (2023–2025)
  - Carried a quota for strategic accounts; consistently above 110% of target.
- Based in Utrecht, Netherlands; prefers remote-first teams
  - Travel fine for team days
- Studied business in the Netherlands, followed by a graduate programme
  - Fluent in Dutch and English
- Career pattern: roughly three years per role
  - Moves when growth stalled, not just for title
  - No gap in the CV, explained by a sabbatical
- Side projects: writes a newsletter
  - Good indicator of community standing

### Possible roles
- No open role in the portfolio that fits right now
  - Worth keeping warm for the next wave of Series A hiring
- Upcoming: Signalbay is planning to open a Sales Manager Benelux role soon
  - Worth flag Lukas to Signalbay early
- Coming up: Annotaire expects to open a Sales Development Representative role in the coming months
  - Worth flag Lukas to Annotaire early
- Outside the portfolio, Lukas has interest from two Series B companies
  - Means we need to move quickly if someone is interested

### Questions they asked
- Asked a lot about runway at the portfolio companies
  - Signals they have been burned before
- Wanted to know how Stroopwafel helps portfolio hires in the first 90 days
  - Pointed them to the portfolio community channel run by {{user:i02}}
- Asked about equity norms at Series A in the Netherlands
  - Gave the usual ranges and the new tax treatment of options
- Asked which founders are best to work for among our companies
  - Kept it high level; suggested specific intros once there is a concrete role
- Wanted to know how fast the company is growing
  - Good questions, showing interest in impact not just perks

### Impressions
- Strengths: mid-market sales plus pipeline building
  - Gave concrete examples with numbers, which is rare
- Watch-outs: short tenures in the last two roles
  - Probe in references
- Communication clear and structured; should do well with technical founders
  - Should probe how they deal with pushback in a working session
- Team fit: good at bringing structure to chaos
  - Could balance a fast-moving founder
- Self-awareness good: was clear about their gaps unprompted
  - Looking for a manager who will coach them on people leadership
- Overall view: good, not yet exceptional
  - Would introduce them to two founders first
  - Our rating: 3.5 out of 5 on the talent scorecard
- Main risk for a founder: could be expensive relative to stage
  - Way to handle it: start with a clear 6-month plan

### Highlights from the conversation
- Walked us through how they took over the mid-market sales function at Pebblepath
  - Moved the headline metric by 26% in four quarters
  - Brought in four people and restructured the old process
- Biggest achievement: cutting churn in half
  - Gave credit to the team generously, which we liked
  - Figures checked out when we pushed for detail
- Something that went wrong: a project they killed too late
  - Lesson: over-communicate with stakeholders
- Comfortable working with founders day to day and presenting to a board
  - Has written a board update on their own
- Customer orientation was obvious: spends time with customers every week
  - Unusual for someone in this function
- Mentioned stopping a launch that was not ready
  - Dealt with it constructively, with data

### How they work
- Has not managed people yet, keen to mentor juniors first
  - Describes their style as direct, with clear goals
- Strongest example: rebuilt an underperforming team in six months
  - Numbers held up when we probed
- Toughest moment: a failed product launch
  - Reflective about what they would do differently
- How they decide: consults the team, then decides
  - Example from a vendor choice
- On feedback: runs regular retros
  - Consistent with what a former colleague told us
- Track record in hiring: promoted three people internally
  - Uses a clear scorecard

### Asks & opportunities
- Lukas asked for intros to companies hiring in mid-market sales.
- Opportunity: Lukas could refer two or three strong people from their network.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:p11}}: add to the talent pool with tags (by 29 Mar)
- [ ] Lukas: send an updated CV (by 29 Mar)
- [ ] {{user:p11}}: add notes to the contact record (by 29 Mar)

  - Recent investments include two AI tooling companies at seed
- Their LPs: mostly family offices and a fund-of-funds
  - Next fund planned in about two years
- Fund life: investing until 2027 with two years of follow-ons

- Polderheat (Series B, climate tech): planning a raise in Q2 2026

### Attendees

- {{user:p15}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Intro call with Tomáš Kovač to understand where they could help portfolio companies. Recommended by a portfolio founder.

### Experience
- Currently Fractional CPO, self-employed (2023–present)
  - Launched the self-serve tier and the first usage-based pricing plan.

- Before that Chief Product Officer at Ticketline Events (2021–2023)
  - Product lead for the payments and billing area.
- Earlier VP Product at Pebblepath (2018–2020)
  - Launched the self-serve tier and the first usage-based pricing plan.
- Based in Krakow, Poland; open to hybrid in Amsterdam
  - Commute fine two or three days a week
- Studied law at a technical university, followed by consulting
  - Fluent in English and French
- Pattern: a mix of scale-ups and one corporate stint
  - Moved when growth stalled, rather than for title
  - One gap in the CV, explained by a sabbatical
- Side projects: organises a meetup
  - Useful signal of community standing

### Portfolio matches
- Plumline: would benefit from a session on board reporting
  - Pre-seed, a vertical CRM
- Klusjesclub: would benefit from a session on the next fundraise
  - Series A, a marketplace for vetted local tradespeople
- Fenceline AI: could use help with hiring a first manager
  - Seed, guardrails and red-teaming for LLM apps

  - Might run it as a workshop for a small group

### Areas of expertise
- Core areas: pricing, user research and B2B product
  - Usually engaged by growth-stage teams
- Strong opinion: roadmaps should be outcome-based once you pass 20 engineers
  - Shared two examples from recent clients
- Point of view: discovery should be a weekly habit, not a phase
  - Gave an example from a previous company
- Strong opinion: usage-based pricing needs a product that makes usage visible
  - Gave an example from recent clients
- Industries of deepest experience: B2B software and fintech

Intro with Wei Kavanagh and Michał Kovač from Fjordline Ventures to explore co-investment opportunities. First proper meeting after a few emails.

- Team of 7 partners and a small investment team
  - Partners cover one or two sectors; investment decisions by consensus
- Portfolio of 44 companies, largely in Northern Europe
  - Latest investments are a payments startup at Series A
- Their LPs: a mix of institutions and founders
  - Next fund planned in about two years
- Fund life: investing until 2027 with two years of follow-ons
  - Deployment pace slightly behind plan because of valuations

### Deal flow from our side
- Fertiel (Series A, health tech): likely raising in Q3 2026
  - Builds fertility and family-forming benefits; they'd like the deck
- Dosewise (seed, health tech): planning a raise in the next six months
  - Builds medication adherence; they asked for an update in a month
- Rosterwell (Series A, B2B SaaS): might raise in the next six months
  - Builds shift planning and workforce scheduling; they'd like an update in a month

### Recent activity
- Fjordline Ventures made 6 new investments in the last twelve months
  - Mostly seed rounds of €2.6m–€6.3m
  - Two follow-ons syndicated with UK funds
- Strongest portfolio companies are in infrastructure
  - Three up-rounds in the past year; one write-down so far
- Platform has become a bigger part of the pitch: talent programmes
  - Interested in joint workshops with {{user:i04}}
- Reserves tighter than they would like for the current fund
  - May need co-investors for larger rounds
- Exits in the current fund: two small acquisitions
  - Distributions below where LPs want it
- Notable portfolio company recently closed a Series B with a London growth fund
  - Positive signal for follow-on demand more broadly

### How they work
- Keen on sharing deal flow where we overlap
  - Want a bi-monthly call between the partnerships
- Process: partner meeting weekly, term sheet within three to five weeks of first meeting
  - Strongly prefer warm intros via co-investors
- Value-add: a founder CFO community
  - Portfolio founders use it a lot, mostly for senior hires
- Reference calls: three founders speak highly of the partner in the room
  - Good to cross-check with portfolio founders who have worked with them
- On boards they are: very involved in hiring
  - Two founders we know describe them as supportive in hard moments
- Usual co-investors: a group of Nordic seed funds
  - Keen on adding more Benelux co-investors

### Working together
- Will swap pipeline every quarter in overlapping sectors
  - Start with: a short list of three to five names each
- Discussed co-hosting a founder dinner together
  - {{user:i04}} to check the calendar for May
- Open to introductions to other Benelux funds
  - Reciprocal, they offered intros to US funds
- Talent collaboration: agreed to share a talent pool for senior roles
  - {{user:i04}} to align with their platform lead
- Agreed a light rule: tell each other early when looking at the same company
  - Avoids awkward competition on shared deals

### Market notes
- They see 25% more Series A decks than last year, mostly AI-related
  - Average quality lower than the volume suggests
- Exits picking up slightly: small trade sales remain the main route
  - Expect more strategic M&A in 2027
- Pricing stable outside AI
  - Boards pushing capital efficiency over growth at all costs
- Co-investment appetite strong for Dutch deals with a credible path to €10m ARR
  - Particularly keen in fintech follow-ons
- AI absorbing most of fresh capital
  - Other companies need clear unit economics to raise
- Secondaries market more active; early employees selling some liquidity in Series B rounds
  - Mixed views on whether it hurts alignment

### Asks & opportunities
- Fjordline Ventures asked to see more climate tech, health tech and B2B SaaS deal flow from us.
- Opportunity: they could be a good follow-on investor for our Series A companies.

body:
### Attendees
- Marloes Veenstra (Partner, Oakmeadow Partners)
- Irene Campos (Associate, Oakmeadow Partners)
- {{user:i03}} (Principal, Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Catch-up with Marloes Veenstra and Irene Campos from Oakmeadow Partners to compare notes on the market. Second conversation this year.

### About the fund
- Oakmeadow Partners is investing from Fund III (€120m), final close in 2025
  - A growth fund leading Series B and C rounds in Europe.
  - About 44% committed so far; pace of 13 new investments a year
- Initial cheques of €1.44m–€4.8m, reserves of 1:1 for follow-ons
  - Like to lead and take a board seat from Series A
- Team of 7 partners and a small investment team
  - Each partner covers one or two sectors; investment decisions by consensus
- Current portfolio of 19 companies, mostly in the UK and DACH
  - Latest investments include two AI tooling companies at seed
- Their LPs: mostly family offices and a fund-of-funds
  - Next fund planned in 2027
- Fund timeline: investing until 2027 with three years of follow-ons
  - Pace on track because of market conditions

### Deal flow from our side
- Rosterwell (Series A, B2B SaaS): likely raising in early 2027
  - Makes shift planning and workforce scheduling; they asked for an update in a month
- Driftmark (seed, fintech): might raise in the next six months
  - Builds embedded insurance APIs; they'd like a first call
- Fennel Payroll (Series A, fintech): planning a raise in the next six months
  - Makes payroll and contractor payments; they asked for a first call

### Ways to collaborate
- Will share deal notes on a regular basis in overlapping sectors
  - Start with: a short list of three to five names each
- Talked about co-hosting a talent evening jointly
  - {{user:i03}} to propose dates for May
- Interested in meeting some of our LPs
  - Reciprocal, they can share intros to US funds
- Talent collaboration: could share a talent pool for senior roles
  - {{user:i03}} to connect with their talent lead
- Discussed a light principle: tell each other early when evaluating the same company
  - Avoids awkward competition on shared deals

### How they see the market
- Seeing 39% more Series A decks than last year, mostly AI-related
  - Average quality mixed
- Exits picking up slightly: small trade sales remain the main route
  - They expect more strategic M&A in 2027
- Valuations bifurcated: AI rounds hot, the rest disciplined
  - Boards pushing capital efficiency over growth at all costs
- Appetite for co-investing strong for Benelux deals with a credible path to €5m ARR
  - Especially keen in fintech follow-ons
- AI absorbing most of new capital
  - Non-AI companies need clear unit economics to raise
- Secondary activity growing; early employees taking some liquidity in later rounds
  - Mixed views on whether it helps alignment

### Investment focus
- Focus areas: fintech, health tech and B2B SaaS
  - Excited about developer tooling for AI agents
- Staying away from consumer in this fund
  - Learned from the last fund: be careful with channel-dependent models
- Their read on the market: seed valuations back to 2019 levels outside AI
  - Their LPs pushing for distributions more than ever
- Target ownership around 12–20% at entry
  - Will go higher for exceptional teams
- Due diligence approach: heavy on customer calls
  - Typically 13 customer calls before investment committee
- A deal they regret missing: a vertical SaaS company that is now a category leader
  - Changed how they weigh founder-market fit
- Deal sourcing mostly via founders and accelerators
  - Cold inbound seldom leads to investments

### Recent activity
- Oakmeadow Partners closed 7 new investments in the last twelve months
  - Mostly Series A rounds of €1.8m–€5.3m
  - One follow-on co-led with Nordic funds
- Best-performing portfolio companies are in vertical software
  - Three markups in the past year; one write-down so far
- Portfolio support has become a bigger part of the pitch: go-to-market workshops
  - Interested in shared workshops with {{user:i03}}
- Follow-on capacity tighter than they would like in the current fund
  - May look for co-investors for later rounds
- Exits in the previous fund: one trade sale
  - Distributions still modest
- A notable portfolio company just raised a Series B with a US growth fund
  - Positive signal for follow-on demand more broadly

### Asks & opportunities
- Oakmeadow Partners asked to see more fintech, health tech and B2B SaaS deal flow from us.
- Opportunity: co-invest in a portfolio company's next round where the focus overlaps.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:i03}}: send the Rosterwell one-pager (by next week)
- [ ] {{user:i03}}: send the Driftmark one-pager (by 3 May)
- [ ] {{user:i03}}: send the Fennel Payroll one-pager (by 3 May)

body:
### Attendees
- Mei El Amrani (Partner, Lantern Peak Capital)
- {{user:i03}} (Principal, Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Catch-up with Mei El Amrani from Lantern Peak Capital to explore co-investment opportunities. Second conversation this year.

### About the fund
- Lantern Peak Capital is investing from Fund IV (€60m), final close in 2026
  - A Series A and B fund backing European software companies.
  - About 64% committed so far; aiming for 11 new investments a year
- Initial cheques of €720k–€2.4m, reserving 1:1 for follow-ons
  - Prefer to co-lead and take a board seat
- Team of 4 partners
  - Partners cover one or two sectors; decisions by consensus
- Current portfolio of 35 companies, mostly in the UK and DACH
  - Recent investments include two AI tooling companies at seed
- LP base: mostly family offices and a fund-of-funds
  - Next fund expected in about two years
- Fund timeline: investing until 2027 plus two years of follow-ons
  - Deployment pace on track given valuations

### Deal flow from our side
- Schemata Labs (pre-seed, developer tools): planning a raise in the next six months
  - Builds safe database schema migrations; they asked for the deck
- Hearthdesk (seed, B2B SaaS): might raise in early 2027
  - Makes property management software; they asked for an update in a month
- Rosterwell (Series A, B2B SaaS): might raise in Q3 2026
  - Builds shift planning and workforce scheduling; they asked for a first call

### How they see the market
- They see 24% more Series A decks than last year, largely AI-related
  - Average quality lower than the volume suggests
- Liquidity still slow: small trade sales remain the main route
  - They expect a few IPO windows in 2027
- Valuations bifurcated: AI rounds hot, the rest disciplined
  - Investors pushing capital efficiency over growth at all costs
- Co-investment appetite high for Dutch deals with a credible path to €10m ARR
  - Particularly keen in climate follow-ons
- AI-native companies taking most of new capital
  - Other founders need clear unit economics to raise
- Secondary market growing; early employees selling small amounts in later rounds
  - Mixed on whether it hurts alignment

### Their portfolio
- Lantern Peak Capital made 8 new investments in the last twelve months
  - Mostly Series A deals of €2.6m–€7.3m
  - Two follow-ons syndicated with UK funds
- Best-performing companies sit in payments
  - Three up-rounds in the past year; one write-down so far
- Platform has become a bigger part of the pitch: talent programmes
  - Interested in shared workshops with {{user:i03}}
- Reserves healthy for the current fund
  - Will look for co-investors for larger rounds
- Liquidity in the current fund: one trade sale
  - DPI below where LPs want it
- A notable company recently closed a Series B led by a US growth fund
  - Good signal for follow-on demand in general

### Investment focus
- Focus areas: B2B SaaS, developer tools and AI infrastructure
  - Spending a lot of time on infrastructure for the energy transition
- Staying away from consumer for now
  - Learned from the last fund: be careful with channel-dependent models
- Their read on the market: Series A bar now ~€3m ARR with strong retention
  - LPs pushing for distributions before re-upping
- Ownership target around 12–20% at entry
  - Will stretch for category leaders
- Due diligence approach: founder references first
  - Typically 8 customer calls before IC
- Anti-portfolio regret: a vertical SaaS company that is now a category leader
  - Shifted how they weigh early traction
- Sourcing largely through founders and accelerators
  - Inbound rarely leads to investments

### Ways to collaborate
- Will share pipeline on a regular basis in overlapping sectors
  - Start with: a shared list of three to five names each
- Discussed co-hosting a founder dinner together
  - {{user:i03}} to propose dates for Q3 2026
- Interested in meeting corporate venture teams we know
  - In return, they can share their talent network
- Hiring overlap: agreed to share a talent pool for senior roles
  - {{user:i03}} to align with their talent lead
- Agreed a light rule: share before term sheets when looking at the same company
  - Prevents unnecessary bidding on overlapping deals

### Asks & opportunities
- Lantern Peak Capital asked to see more B2B SaaS, developer tools and AI infrastructure deal flow from us.
- Opportunity: a joint founder event in Q3 2026.

### Next steps

- [ ] {{user:i03}}: send the Rosterwell one-pager (by 27 Jun)

  - Startups seen as a way to move faster
- Targets tied to the programme are published internally
  - Progress reviewed quarterly by the board
- Leadership changed last year, with a new CEO who is pushing for speed
  - Opportunity for new partners while priorities are being set

### Portfolio fit
- Pulsebridge Labs: could help with IT and procurement
  - Builds clinical trial patient matching; they'd want a sponsor in the business
- Mendwell: relevant for operating-room planning
  - Offers digital physiotherapy for back and joint pain; they'd want a sponsor in the business
- Ateliermarkt: could help with the cardiology department
  - Builds a booking marketplace for creative studios; worth a first call
- Also interested in AI tools for internal teams even if outside the core brief
  - No budget yet, but could run a test in Q4 2026
- Prefer one or two high-quality intros over a long list
  - Each intro should include a one-pager and a named use case

  - To scan the portfolio and revert within two weeks

### Org & stakeholders
- Hannah reports into the COO's office
  - Mandate: can open doors but cannot sign
- Suggested we also speak to Diego Bianchi (Medical Director)
  - Close to the budget for the pilots we discussed
- Recent reorganisation shifted innovation under the CFO
  - Some uncertainty about budgets for 2027
- Influence lies with business units more than the innovation team
  - Best path: start with one country
- The CTO office has a strong say on any integration
  - Worth meet them before the pilot

### Previous startup collaborations
- Ran 7 startup pilots in the last two years, mostly in IT
  - Just 2 turned into production deployments
  - Successful ones had a business owner from day one
- Most successful collaboration: a scheduling tool now used across the company
  - Took nine months from pilot to full contract
- Failed pilots usually stalled at IT security
  - The team now pre-approve vendor paperwork
- Buying from startups now a formal programme with a small team
  - Team sits under strategy

### Budget and decision-making
- Innovation budget for 2027 about €600k
  - BUs must co-fund anything beyond a pilot
- Sign-off needs the BU director for anything above €50k
  - Steering committee convenes every six weeks
- Ideal timing for new pilots: during the autumn planning round
  - Last-minute proposals rarely make it into the plan
- Payment terms: 60 days by default; shorter terms possible for small vendors
  - Important to flag early for cash-sensitive companies
- Longer contracts require board approval over €250k
  - Small pilots may be approved locally

### Pilot & procurement process
- Pilots need a business sponsor and a multi-week security review
  - Paid pilots capped at around €70k
- Vendor onboarding via central procurement takes 6 weeks
  - Advice: get on the preferred-supplier list early
- Planning cycle closes in the autumn; new initiatives must be in the plan by then
  - Out-of-cycle requests need an executive sponsor
- Innovation team is small and acts as a door-opener to the business units
  - Good entry point, but business units own the budgets
- Pilot success judged by time saved within 13 weeks
  - Criteria agreed up front with the business owner
- IT security checklist has over 150 questions; ISO 27001 shortcuts most of it
  - Hosting must stay in the EU
- Legal uses a framework agreement; liability caps are the usual sticking point
  - Advice: flag deviations early
- References are essential: they ask for a comparable customer before signing
  - Portfolio companies with strong Benelux references have an edge

### Asks & opportunities
- Rivierland Hospital Group wants a shortlist of startups for their 2027 plan.
- Hannah asked for a contact at a peer fund.

- [ ] {{user:p14}}: send a short intro note on Mendwell (by 23 Aug)
- [ ] Hannah: share the pilot criteria document (by 20 Aug)

  - Collections healthy; DSO around 45 days
  - Treasury moved to a higher-yield account at the house bank

title: Saltmarsh Ventures x Stroopwafel
summary: Met Saltmarsh Ventures to compare notes and share deal flow; shared Patchyard, Cobble API and Flagpost as potential deals.
body:
### Attendees
- Marek Horváth (General Partner, Saltmarsh Ventures)
- Floor van Dam (Associate, Saltmarsh Ventures)
- {{user:i02}} (General Partner, Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Catch-up with Marek Horváth and Floor van Dam from Saltmarsh Ventures to compare notes on the market. Second conversation this year.

### About the fund
- Saltmarsh Ventures deploying Fund II (€450m), first close in 2023
  - A technical-founder fund backing developer tools and infrastructure.
  - About 52% committed so far; pace of 11 new investments a year
- Initial cheques of €5.4m–€18m, reserves of about 1.5x for follow-ons
  - Like to lead and take a board seat
- Team of 5 partners and a small investment team
  - Each partner covers two sectors; investment decisions by consensus
- Current portfolio of 30 companies, mostly in Northern Europe
  - Recent investments are a grid-software company at seed
- Their LPs: a corporate anchor plus private investors
  - Next fund planned in 2027
- Fund life: investment period runs to 2027 with two years of follow-ons
  - Deployment pace slightly behind plan because of market conditions

### Our companies raising
- Patchyard (Series A, developer tools): likely raising in Q4 2026
  - Builds dependency and supply-chain security; they asked for the deck
- Cobble API (seed, developer tools): planning a raise in early 2027
  - Builds API mocking and contract testing; they asked for a first call
- Flagpost (seed, developer tools): might raise in the next six months
  - Builds feature flags and progressive delivery; they asked for a first call

### How they work
- Open to sharing deal flow where we overlap
  - Would like a quarterly call between the investment teams
- Process: partner meeting every Monday, typically four to six weeks of first meeting
  - Strongly prefer warm intros via founders they know
- Value-add: talent network and an executive search partner
  - Portfolio founders use it a lot, especially for first US hires
- Reference calls: three founders recommend the partner in the room
  - Good to cross-check with portfolio founders who have worked with them
- On boards they are: very involved in hiring
  - Founders describe them as demanding but fair
- Co-investors: US funds at Series B
  - Keen on adding more Benelux partners

### Ways to collaborate
- Agreed to swap deal notes every quarter in overlapping sectors
  - First step: a short list of companies we are both tracking
- Discussed co-hosting a talent evening together
  - {{user:i02}} to propose dates for October
- Interested in introductions to other Benelux funds
  - In return, they can share their talent network
- Talent overlap: could share candidates for exec roles
  - {{user:i02}} to connect with their talent lead
- Agreed a simple rule: share before term sheets when evaluating the same company
  - Prevents awkward bidding on shared deals

### Market notes
- They see about a third more seed decks than last year, largely AI-related
  - Average quality mixed
- Liquidity still slow: secondaries remain the main route
  - Expect more strategic M&A in 2027
- Valuations bifurcated: AI rounds hot, the rest disciplined
  - Boards pushing capital efficiency and burn multiples
- Co-investment appetite high for Dutch deals with a clear path to €10m ARR
  - Especially keen in B2B software deals
- AI-native companies taking most of new capital
  - Other companies must show clear unit economics to raise
- Secondary market more active; early employees taking some liquidity in Series B rounds
  - Mixed on whether it helps retention

### Thesis & focus
- Focus areas: developer tools and AI infrastructure
  - Spending a lot of time on vertical software with embedded payments
- Staying away from businesses that depend on a single channel in this fund
  - Lesson from a write-off: avoid channel-dependent models
- Market view: Series A bar now ~€2m ARR with strong retention
  - LPs asking about DPI more than ever
- Ownership target around 12–20% at entry
  - Happy to go higher for exceptional teams
- Due diligence style: data-room driven
  - Usually 15 customer calls before investment committee
- Anti-portfolio regret: a vertical SaaS company that is now a category leader
  - Shifted how they think about early traction
- Deal sourcing largely through scouts and university spin-outs
  - Cold inbound seldom results in investments

### Asks & opportunities
- Saltmarsh Ventures asked to see more developer tools and AI infrastructure deal flow from us.
- Opportunity: swap notes on two companies we are both tracking.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:i02}}: send the Patchyard one-pager (by 9 Sep)
- [ ] {{user:i02}}: send the Cobble API one-pager (by 9 Sep)
- [ ] {{user:i02}}: send the Flagpost one-pager (by 9 Sep)

### Context

title: Meeting with Ashgrove Strategy Partners
summary: Meeting with Ashgrove Strategy Partners about their priorities and how they run pilots with startups.
body:
### Attendees
- Jeroen Haverkamp (Engagement Manager, Ashgrove Strategy Partners)
- Eleni Kaya (Partner, Ashgrove Strategy Partners)
- {{user:p14}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Follow-up meeting with Jeroen Haverkamp and Eleni Kaya from Ashgrove Strategy Partners about their startup programme. Set up after an intro from a portfolio founder.

### Strategic priorities
- Top priority: an ecosystem of startup partners
  - Programme budget of roughly €1.6m this year
  - Board-level sponsor in place
- Also: AI transformation work for clients
  - Programme budget around €500k this year
  - Executive attention in place
- Another priority: energy-transition practice growth
  - Budget around €2.5m this year
  - Executive sponsor in place
- Executive pressure on growth in new segments for 2027
  - Startups positioned as a way to test ideas cheaply
- KPIs tied to these priorities are set at board level
  - Status checked quarterly by the board
- The leadership team changed recently, bringing a new COO who is pushing for speed
  - Window for new partners before budgets are locked

### Relevant portfolio companies
- Pallet Atlas: relevant for the digital transformation practice
  - Builds warehouse operations software; worth a first call
- Dosewise: could help with the digital transformation practice
  - Builds medication adherence; worth a first call
- Kliniq Flow: could help with the energy practice
  - Builds operating-room scheduling; they'd want a sponsor in the business
- Also interested in sustainability reporting as a second track
  - Small budget for now, but might join a pilot in Q4 2026
- Want a small number of well-prepared intros over a long list
  - Each intro should come with a short case and a named use case
- Also requested ideas for startups in workforce scheduling
  - Will scan the wider network and revert within two weeks

### How decisions get made
- Innovation budget for 2027 about €1.1m
  - Business units co-fund pilots
- Sign-off needs a steering committee for anything above €50k
  - Steering committee convenes every six weeks
- Best timing for new proposals: in the first quarter
  - Late proposals rarely get funded
- Payment terms: 45 days standard; faster terms possible for startups
  - Worth raise up front for cash-sensitive companies
- Longer contracts need board approval above €500k
  - Pilots may be approved locally

### Previous startup collaborations
- Have run 3 startup pilots in the last two years, mostly in operations
  - Just 3 turned into contracts
  - The ones that worked had a business owner from day one
- Most successful collaboration: an analytics vendor that replaced an incumbent
  - Took twelve months from pilot to rollout
- Failed pilots mostly stalled at the budget round
  - The team now involve procurement earlier
- Buying from startups is on the agenda with a small team
  - Team sits under strategy

### Working with them
- Pilots need a business sponsor and a multi-week security review
  - Pilot budgets capped at around €40k
- Vendor onboarding via central procurement takes 6 weeks
  - Tip: start onboarding in parallel with the pilot
- Planning cycle closes in November; new initiatives must be in the plan by then
  - Out-of-cycle requests require an executive sponsor
- Innovation team is two people and acts as a broker to the business units
  - Good first contact, but the BUs own the budgets
- Success judged by time saved within 13 weeks
  - Criteria agreed before the pilot starts with the sponsor
- IT security questionnaire has ~200 questions; ISO 27001 shortcuts most of it
  - Hosting must stay in the EU
- Contracting uses their own templates; liability caps take the longest
  - Advice: send redlines in one round
- Reference customers are essential: they ask for two Dutch references ahead of any pilot
  - Our companies with good local references have an edge

### Open questions & concerns
- Concern about data residency for critical processes
  - Mitigation: EU-only hosting
- Past startup collaborations: 3 pilots in two years, two made it to a contract
  - Why: integration costs
- Their legal team requires their own contract templates even for pilots
  - Their template is fairly heavy on liability; expect two rounds of comments
- Worried about change management during a pilot
  - Want startups that bring implementation support
- Reputation risk with consumer-facing pilots
  - Prefer internal use cases to start with

### Asks & opportunities
- Ashgrove Strategy Partners wants a shortlist of startups for their 2027 plan.
- Jeroen asked for a benchmark of how other corporates run pilots.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:p14}}: send a short intro note on Pallet Atlas (by 11 Sep)
- [ ] {{user:p14}}: send a short intro note on Dosewise (by next week)
- [ ] Jeroen: share the pilot criteria document (by 10 Sep)

- {{user:p04}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
First conversation with Sanne Lin, whom we met at a community event. Exploring next steps and possible roles in the portfolio. Goal was to understand what they want next and where they could fit.

### Profile

  - Commute fine two or three days a week
- Has a degree in law in the Netherlands, then a graduate programme
  - Speaks Dutch and English
- Career pattern: roughly three years per role
  - Moved for the team, rather than for title
  - One gap in the CV
- Side projects: angel invests small tickets
  - Good indicator of network

### Possible roles
- Carbonwick: Head of Engineering (Copenhagen) is a strong fit
  - Relevant experience in hiring engineers and engineering leadership
  - Carbonwick is a seed climate tech company with 11-50 people
- Windvane Grid: Head of Engineering (Amsterdam) is a partial fit
  - Seniority a bit below what they want
  - Windvane Grid is a Series A climate tech company with 51-200 people
- Grachtpay: Head of Engineering (Amsterdam) is a strong fit
  - Directly relevant experience in hiring engineers and engineering leadership
  - Grachtpay is a Series B fintech company with 51-200 people
