  - Worth flag Sanne to Signalbay before the role goes live
- Coming up: Mossgrid expects to open a Mobile Engineer (iOS) role soon
  - Worth mention Sanne to Mossgrid before the role goes live
- Outside the portfolio, Sanne is also talking to two Series B companies
  - So we should move quickly if a founder is interested

### Back-channel options
- Overlapped with Jeroen Kuipers at Ovenfresh
  - Jeroen is now Co-founder & CTO at Sluisline; could be a reference
- Overlapped with Charlotte Hendriks at Lowland Telecom
  - Charlotte is now Co-founder & CTO at Hearthdesk; worth asking for a back-channel

### What they're looking for
- Wants a step up into a lead role at a growth-stage company
  - Sectors of interest: hiring engineers, engineering leadership and food delivery
  - Wants a clear path to leadership more than title
- Motivation for moving: the company is restructuring
  - Not in a hurry, but would move quickly for the right role
- Team size: a team of five to fifteen
  - Has not built a team from zero so far
  - Likes hands-on roles to pure management
- Where: happy in Amsterdam, Rotterdam or Utrecht
  - Occasional travel no problem up to a week a month
- Red flags for them: no clear product-market fit
  - Wants to see runway and burn before an offer
- Preferred stage: first 50 employees, preferably B2B

  - Not keen on consumer businesses

- Industries they would rather avoid: none in particular
  - Cares about the product being useful beyond the role
- Has a view on which of our companies they would like to meet
  - Mentioned a couple of companies they had read about

### Notable work
- Described how they rebuilt a struggling team at Ovenfresh
  - Improved the main metric by 66% in four quarters
  - Brought in five people and restructured the reporting line
- Biggest win: a launch that became a top-three revenue line
  - Credited the team generously, which we liked
  - Figures checked out when we pushed for detail
- Something that went wrong: a hire that did not work out
  - Lesson: over-communicate with stakeholders
- Experienced working with founders directly and presenting to a board
  - Has not yet written a board section themselves
- Customer orientation came through: built a customer council
  - Rare for this level
- Mentioned stopping a launch that was not ready
  - Dealt with it calmly, with a clear alternative

### Their questions
- Asked a lot about founder dynamics at the portfolio companies
  - Good sign they have been burned before
- Asked how Stroopwafel helps portfolio hires after joining
  - Pointed them to the operator community run by {{user:p04}}
- Asked about equity norms at this stage in the Netherlands
  - Shared rough ranges and the current tax treatment of options
- Asked which founders are best to work for among our companies
  - Stayed general; suggested specific intros once there is a concrete role
- Wanted to know how fast the company is growing
  - Sharp question, showing interest in the team not just perks

### Asks & opportunities
- Sanne asked for intros to companies hiring in hiring engineers.
- Opportunity: Sanne could refer a few strong people from their network.

### Context

### Fund overview
- Lantern Peak Capital is investing from Fund IV (€450m), first close in 2026
  - A Series A and B fund backing European software companies.

- First cheques of €5.4m–€18m, reserving 1:1 for follow-ons
  - Like to lead and take a board seat from Series A
- Team of 4 partners plus a platform lead
  - Partners cover two sectors; investment decisions by majority
- Current portfolio of 29 companies, mostly in Northern Europe
  - Latest investments are a grid-software company at seed
- LP base: a corporate anchor plus private investors
  - Fund raising expected in 2027
- Fund timeline: investing until 2027 with two years of follow-ons
  - Deployment pace slightly behind plan because of market conditions

### Our companies raising
- Fenceline AI (seed, AI infrastructure): planning a raise in Q4 2026
  - Builds guardrails and red-teaming for LLM apps; they asked for a first call
- Computesluis (pre-seed, AI infrastructure): might raise in the next six months
  - Builds GPU scheduling across clouds; they'd like a first call
- Cobble API (seed, developer tools): planning a raise in Q4 2026

### Investment focus
- Focus areas: B2B SaaS, developer tools and AI infrastructure
  - Excited about developer tooling for AI agents
- Staying away from businesses that depend on a single channel for now
  - Lesson from the last fund: avoid capital-heavy models
- Market view: Series A bar now ~€2m ARR with strong retention
  - Their LPs pushing for DPI before re-upping
- Ownership target of 8–12% at entry
  - Will stretch for exceptional teams
- Due diligence style: data-room driven
  - Usually two weeks of DD before IC
- A deal they regret missing: a vertical SaaS company that is now a category leader
  - Shifted how they weigh founder-market fit
- Sourcing largely through scouts and university spin-outs

  - {{user:i01}} explained the founder community
- Curious about our Benelux deal flow
  - Shared a quick view; they shared theirs on UK valuations

- Wanted our view on exit routes for Benelux companies
  - Gave examples from the latest portfolio hires

title: Refurbo: Q3 2026 check-in
summary: Refurbo check-in: ARR at €905k (+31% QoQ) and Series A planned for Q3 2027. Main needs: deals with insurers stalling at pilot-to-contract conversion, Senior Account Executive gap and a future Head of Customer Success.
body:
### Attendees
- Jeroen Lammers (CEO & Co-founder, Refurbo)
- Inès Szabó (Co-founder & COO, Refurbo)
- {{user:i02}} (General Partner, Stroopwafel Ventures)
- {{user:p07}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Scheduled check-in with Jeroen Lammers and Inès Szabó. We covered KPIs, go-to-market and people & hiring.

### KPIs
- Run-rate revenue landed at €905k, up 31% versus last quarter
  - 51 new customers in the quarter; largest new contract €17k ACV
  - About 6% ahead of the board plan of €853k, mostly thanks to a bigger-than-expected expansion at their largest customer
- Burn running at €73k/month, runway until May 2028 (20 months)
  - Gross margin at 63%
  - The plan keeps the burn multiple below 1.3x
- GMV of €679k last month at a 13% take rate
  - Repeat buyers now 60% of GMV
  - Supply is the constraint in peak weeks
- Net revenue retention holding at 120%
  - Expansion driven by B2B accounts
  - 3 customers churned: seasonal drop-off
- Cash in the bank at €1.46m
  - Receivables slightly slower; DSO around 44 days
  - Treasury moved to a higher-yield account at the house bank
- 166 customers at an average contract value of €5k
  - Top 10 customers are 44% of revenue, down from 68% a year ago
- Month-on-month revenue growth averaged 10% over the quarter
  - Best month was August, thanks to a large expansion

### Go-to-market
- Deals with large insurers tend to stall at pilot-to-contract conversion
  - Happened twice this quarter, most recently with Dijkwacht Insurance
  - Jeroen thinks they are talking to the wrong level
- Weighted pipeline of €420k for Q4 2026, and 6 deals in the final stages
  - Largest opportunity: Dijkwacht Insurance at ~€34k; champion is Esmee van Leeuwen (Financial Controller)
  - Win rate 19% over the last two quarters
- Sales cycle currently 13 days, roughly stable
  - Security reviews add two to three weeks on larger deals
- Inbound now roughly 40% of new pipeline
  - Content and community are doing most of the work
  - Cold outbound works best with production companies
- Competition: losing most often to offline agencies
  - They win when local support matters; they lose on brand recognition
  - Dropped two deals this quarter on price alone
- Sales team: one AE ramped, founders still doing most discovery calls
  - Quota attainment around 71% for ramped reps
  - New sales manager started in September
- ACV on new deals up to €7k
  - Larger deals come with longer pilots
- Self-serve trials at 149 a month, 6% converting to paid
  - Activation still too slow for smaller teams

### People & hiring
- Jeroen is still covering most of the sales work personally while the Senior Account Executive seat is open
  - It is affecting pipeline coverage
- Team at 13 FTE, plan to reach 16 by the end of Q4 2026
  - Attrition low this year
- Closed the Growth Marketer hire; starts in September
  - Search took eight weeks from posting to signed offer
- Senior Account Executive (Eindhoven): open for 1 week
  - 3 candidates in process, none at offer yet
  - Struggling with candidates wanting a higher base than budgeted
- Senior Full-Stack Engineer (Eindhoven): live for 5 weeks
  - 4 candidates in process, one at final round
  - Struggling with finding people with the right infrastructure depth
- {{user:p07}} will support calibrating the scorecard
  - First call with the hiring manager planned for 8 Oct
- Comp bands due a refresh; option pool top-up needed before Q4 2026
  - Current pool has ~2.8% unallocated
- Recruiting mostly in-house
  - Referrals account for 29% of hires this year
  - Time to hire about 51 days
- New-joiner onboarding still ad hoc; buddy system planned
  - New joiners rate onboarding 7/10, up from last quarter

### What shipped
- Shipped dynamic pricing
  - Adoption at 47% of active customers in the first month
  - Customer feedback positive overall; main request is expansion to two new cities
- Released invoicing and payouts inside the platform
  - It took 3 weeks with two engineers
- Next priority: managed service for larger customers
  - Aiming for end of Q4 2026
  - Tight with the current team; might slip by a few weeks
- Spending ~29% of engineering time on paying down technical debt
  - Customer-facing incidents down from 5 to 3 per month
  - Inès wants to protect that time even when sales asks for features
- Shipped a first version of AI assistance for first-line support questions
  - Plan is to include it for free until usage is proven
  - Early users report saving roughly 3 hours a week
- Customer advisory board ran in August with five customers
  - Most requested: role-based permissions
  - Surfaced a reporting gap the team had underestimated
- Engineering team at 32 people in three squads
  - Deploys several times a day, lead time improving

### Regulatory & compliance
- Payment-licensing questions for payouts: on track for Q4 2026
  - External counsel costing €21k
  - Main risk: regulator timelines could push it by a few months
- Also tracking platform-worker rules
  - Not urgent yet, but it will come up in due diligence
- Risk and compliance owner sits with Jeroen for now
  - Wants a dedicated hire next year
- Data-protection reviews come up in most enterprise deals
  - Standard questionnaire answers saves about a week per deal

### Founder check-in
- Jeroen feeling stretched
  - Still spending ~45% of the week on sales
  - Wants to hand over day-to-day sales by Q4 2026
- Co-founder dynamics good; clearer split of responsibilities between Jeroen and Inès
  - Fortnightly founder 1:1 reintroduced
- Considering an executive coach
  - {{user:i02}} to share a shortlist
- Leadership team still uneven: most effective in engineering, weakest in finance
  - Upcoming leadership hire likely in that area
- Asked for advice on letting go of an early employee
  - {{user:i02}} offered to connect them with a founder who did the same
- Taking a proper holiday in October; the leadership team can cover
  - {{user:i02}} strongly encouraged it

### Asks & opportunities
- Not an explicit ask: they lack a relationship with decision makers at insurers like Dijkwacht Insurance; someone who knows how they buy would help.
- Implied: the open Senior Account Executive seat is costing founder time; strong names would be welcome even without a formal ask.
- Will need a Head of Customer Success early next year; early names welcome.

### Next steps

- [ ] {{user:p07}}: share a few profiles for the Senior Account Executive role (by end of month)
- [ ] Jeroen: circulate the budget draft (by 9 Oct)

title: Lowland Telecom: partnerships meeting
summary: Meeting with Lowland Telecom about their priorities and how they run pilots with startups.
body:
### Attendees
- Yasmin Zieliński (Senior Account Executive, Lowland Telecom)
- Mikkel Berglund (Head of Sales, Lowland Telecom)
- {{user:p16}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)
- {{user:p12}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Meeting with Yasmin Zieliński and Mikkel Berglund from Lowland Telecom about working with portfolio companies. Set up after an intro from a portfolio founder.

### Strategic priorities
- Top priority: B2B bundles for SMEs
  - Programme budget of roughly €2.6m for 2027
  - Board-level attention still being secured
- Another priority: network energy efficiency
  - Programme budget around €600k this year
  - Executive sponsor still being secured
- Another priority: IoT connectivity for business customers
  - Budget of roughly €1.3m this year
  - Executive sponsor in place
- Board focus on growth in new segments for 2027
  - External partners positioned as a way to move faster
- Targets linked to the programme are published internally
  - Progress checked every six months by the executive committee
- Leadership was reshuffled last year, with a new CEO who is pushing for speed
  - Window for new partners while priorities are being set

### Possible matches
- Clausewise: relevant for the IoT business unit
  - Offers contract lifecycle management; worth a first call
- Mendwell: relevant for procurement for SME products
  - Builds digital physiotherapy for back and joint pain; worth a first call
- Hearthdesk: relevant for the IoT business unit
  - Offers property management software; worth a first call
- Also interested in sustainability reporting even if outside the core brief
  - No budget for now, but might run a test in Q4 2026
- Prefer a small number of well-prepared intros over a long list
  - Every intro should come with a short case and a clear use case
- Separately requested a list of startups in workforce scheduling
  - Will scan the portfolio and revert within two weeks

### How they work with startups
- Pilots need a business sponsor and a multi-week security review
  - Pilot budgets capped at around €70k
- Vendor onboarding via central procurement takes 6 weeks
  - Tip: start onboarding in parallel with the pilot
- Planning cycle closes in the autumn; new initiatives must be in the plan by then
  - Late requests need special approval
- Innovation team is small and acts as a door-opener to the business units
  - Useful first contact, but business units hold the budgets
- Pilot success judged by NPS within 13 weeks
  - Criteria agreed before the pilot starts with the business owner
- IT security checklist has over 150 questions; ISO 27001 helps a lot
  - Hosting must stay in the EU
- Contracting uses a framework agreement; IP clauses are the usual sticking point
  - Advice: send redlines in one round
- References matter a lot: they want a comparable customer ahead of any pilot
  - Portfolio companies with good Benelux references stand out

### What has worked before
- Ran 12 startup pilots in the last two years, mostly in sustainability
  - Only 2 became production deployments
  - Successful ones had a budget holder from day one
- Best partnership: an analytics vendor that replaced an incumbent
  - Needed twelve months from pilot to rollout
- Stalled pilots mostly stalled at procurement
  - The team has started to pre-approve vendor paperwork
- Buying from startups now a formal programme with a small team
  - Programme reports to strategy

### How decisions get made
- Innovation budget for 2027 roughly €2.1m, ring-fenced
  - BUs co-fund anything beyond a pilot
- Decision makers sits with a steering committee for anything above €100k
  - The committee convenes monthly
- Best timing for new pilots: during the autumn planning round
  - Late proposals almost never make it into the plan
- Payment terms: 60 days by default; faster terms negotiable for small vendors
  - Worth flag up front for smaller companies
- Longer contracts need board approval above €250k
  - Pilots may be approved by the BU director

### Concerns
- Worry about startup longevity for critical processes
  - Answer: a Stroopwafel intro to the founders
- Previous startup collaborations: a handful of pilots, two made it to a contract
  - Why: budget not planned
- Legal insists on a full security questionnaire even for pilots
  - Their template is fairly one-sided on IP; expect three rounds of comments
- Worried about change management during a pilot
  - Want startups that can work with their IT partner
- Brand risk with consumer-facing pilots
  - Want back-office use cases to start with

### Asks & opportunities
- Lowland Telecom wants a shortlist of startups for their 2027 plan.
- Yasmin asked for a contact at a peer fund.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:p16}}: send a short intro note on Clausewise (by next week)
- [ ] {{user:p16}}: send a short intro note on Mendwell (by 7 Oct)
- [ ] Yasmin: share the pilot criteria document (by 12 Oct)

  - Should probe how they handle pushback in a case
- Team fit: high ownership
  - Would complement a visionary founder
- Self-awareness good: named what they still need to learn without prompting
  - Looking for a manager who will coach them on strategy
- Overall view: good, not yet exceptional
  - Will share the profile with one or two founders first
  - Score: 4 out of 5 on the talent scorecard
- Risk for a hiring manager: limited experience at very early stage
  - Way to handle it: start with a clear 6-month plan

### Working style
- No direct reports so far, keen to mentor juniors first
  - Describes their style as coaching-heavy
- Strongest example: ran the process that cut onboarding time in half
  - The numbers were credible when we probed
- Toughest moment: a failed product launch
  - Reflective about their part in it
- How they decide: data first, then gut
  - Example from a vendor choice
- Feedback culture: runs regular retros
  - Matches what their reference told us
- Track record in hiring: most hires still at the company
  - Relies on work samples

### What's next
- Looking for a step up into a broader remit at a Series A–B company
  - Sectors of interest: engineering leadership, TypeScript and DevOps
  - Wants founders who listen above all
- Motivation for moving: wants to work closer to customers
  - No rush, but has started a few processes
- Team size: a team of five to fifteen
  - Has hired a team from zero before
  - Likes hands-on roles to pure management
- Where: happy in Amsterdam, Rotterdam or Utrecht
  - Occasional travel no problem up to a week a month
- Dealbreakers: unclear funding runway
  - Wants to see the latest board update before an offer
- Preferred stage: Series A to B, ideally B2B
  - Experienced the 20-to-100 transition before and liked it
  - Not keen on large corporates
- Ideal start: listening tour then a plan
  - Expects explicit goals from the CEO in week one
- Domains to avoid: none in particular
  - Cares about impact beyond the role
- Has opinions on which portfolio companies they would like to meet
  - Named two companies from our website

### Stories that stood out
- Described how they rebuilt a struggling team at Willowcare
  - Moved the headline metric by 70% in two quarters
  - Hired four people and replaced the reporting line
- Biggest achievement: cutting churn in half
  - Gave credit to the team without being asked, a good sign
  - Numbers checked out when we pushed for detail
- Something that went wrong: a project they killed too late
  - What they learned: set kill criteria up front
- Comfortable working with a CEO day to day and presenting to a board
  - Has not yet presented a board update on their own
- Customer focus came through: sits in on sales calls
  - Rare for someone in this function
- Mentioned stopping a launch that was not ready
  - Handled it calmly, with a clear alternative

### Asks & opportunities
- Oliver asked for intros to companies hiring in engineering leadership.
- Opportunity: Oliver could refer two or three strong people from their network.

### Next steps

- [ ] {{user:p11}}: intro Oliver to Tallyhaven for the Security Engineer role (by next week)
- [ ] {{user:p11}}: intro Oliver to Mendwell for the Site Reliability Engineer role (by 10 Oct)

title: Dijkwacht Insurance: partnerships meeting
summary: Meeting with Dijkwacht Insurance about their priorities and how they run pilots with startups.
body:
### Attendees
- Juliana Tanaka (Director of Engineering, Dijkwacht Insurance)
- Teun van Dam (Head of Partnerships, Dijkwacht Insurance)
- {{user:p08}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Intro meeting with Juliana Tanaka and Teun van Dam from Dijkwacht Insurance about their priorities for next year. They asked for the meeting after seeing our portfolio update.

### What they care about
- Number one priority: digital distribution
  - Budget of roughly €1.7m for 2027
  - Executive attention in place
- Also: claims automation
  - Programme budget around €2.7m for 2027
  - Executive sponsor in place
- Another priority: prevention services
  - Programme budget of roughly €1.6m for 2027
  - Executive sponsor still being secured
- Board pressure on cost reduction for 2027
  - External partners positioned as a way to move faster
- Targets tied to the programme are published internally
  - Status reviewed every six months by the board
- The leadership team changed recently, with a new digital lead who is pushing for speed
  - Opportunity for new partners while priorities are being set

### Relevant portfolio companies
- Sluisline: relevant for the health-insurance purchasing team
  - Offers KYB and compliance automation; worth a first call
- Quaycredit: could help with the health-insurance purchasing team
  - Builds revenue-based financing; they'd want a sponsor in the business
- Evalgarden: could help with distribution partnerships
  - Builds model evaluation and regression testing; they'd want a sponsor in the business
- Also interested in workforce planning as a second track
  - Small budget yet, but could run a test in Q1 2027
- Want a small number of well-prepared intros over a long list
  - Each intro should come with a one-pager and a clear use case
- Also asked for ideas for startups in energy management
  - Will scan the wider network and come back by 11 Oct

### Previous startup collaborations
- Ran 10 startup pilots in the last two years
  - Only 2 became production deployments
  - Successful ones had a business owner from day one
- Best collaboration: a scheduling tool now used across the company
  - Needed twelve months from pilot to rollout
- Stalled pilots mostly died at the budget round
  - The team now involve procurement earlier
- Venture clienting is a formal programme with one dedicated person
  - Team reports to IT

### Org & stakeholders
- Juliana reports into the strategy team
  - Mandate: owns a small pilot budget
- Recommended Esmee van Leeuwen (Financial Controller)
  - Owns the operational problem for the pilots we discussed
- Recent reorganisation moved partnerships under the COO
  - Some uncertainty about budgets for 2027
- Decision-making lies with business units rather than the innovation team
  - Best path: land a small paid pilot
- Their CTO office holds a veto on any integration
  - Good idea to meet them early

### Risks they raised
- Concern about startup longevity for critical processes
  - Answer: a Stroopwafel intro to the founders
- Past startup collaborations: 2 pilots in two years, two scaled
  - Main reason: budget not planned
- Their legal team requires a full security questionnaire even for pilots
  - Template is one-sided on IP; plan for two rounds of comments
- Worried about internal capacity during a rollout
  - Want startups that can work with their IT partner
- Brand risk with customer-facing pilots
  - Want internal use cases first

### Budget & timing
- Innovation budget for 2027 about €1.8m, not yet approved
  - BUs co-fund pilots
- Sign-off needs the CFO for anything above €100k
  - Steering committee convenes every six weeks
- Ideal timing for new proposals: in the first quarter
  - Late proposals rarely make it into the plan
- Payment terms: 45 days standard; shorter terms possible for small vendors
  - Worth raise up front for cash-sensitive companies
- Longer commitments need board approval above €250k
  - Pilots may be approved locally

### Asks & opportunities
- Dijkwacht Insurance wants a shortlist of startups for their next pilot round.
- Juliana asked for a contact at a peer fund.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:p08}}: send a short intro note on Sluisline (by 11 Oct)
- [ ] {{user:p08}}: send a short intro note on Quaycredit (by 11 Oct)
- [ ] Juliana: share the pilot criteria document (by 12 Oct)

  - New sales manager started in October

- A large medtech incumbent cut prices last month

- Next board meeting scheduled for 14 Nov

- Option grants for recent hires to be approved at the next meeting
  - The pool is getting tight for the hiring plan
- Budget for 2027 built on 105% revenue growth and 18 net new hires

### Capital plan
- Runway to November 2027; planning to raise a Series B of around €32m in Q1 2027
  - Target metrics for the round: €6.56m ARR with growth above 13% QoQ

  - Michał Kovač (Fjordline Ventures) reached out after the last update
  - Wants to run a tight process: six weeks from first meetings to term sheet
- Stroopwafel will likely take its pro-rata
  - {{user:i02}} to discuss with the partnership
- Considering a revenue-based facility to extend runway by six months
  - Two lenders have sent indicative terms
- Valuation expectations realistic: a step up of ~2x on the last round
  - {{user:i02}} suggested a clean structure matters more than headline valuation
- Data room about 60% ready; cohort analysis needs work
  - Target is to have it ready six weeks before the first meetings

### Commercial traction
- Annualised revenue at €3.65m, up 17% quarter on quarter
  - 12 new customers in the quarter; biggest new contract €91k ACV
  - About 18% ahead of the board plan of €3.1m, helped by an early renewal with expansion
- 6,616 active patients across 79 contracted sites
  - 90-day adherence around 65%
- Cash in the bank at €2.64m
  - Collections slightly slower; DSO at 57 days
  - Debt facility untouched; kept as a buffer
- Net revenue retention at 116%
  - Growth within accounts driven by insurer contracts adding members
  - Zero churned logos; one downgrade
- 79 paying customers at an average contract value of €46k
  - Top 10 customers are 58% of revenue, down from 64% a year ago
- Net burn running at €203k/month, runway until November 2027 (13 months)
  - Gross margin at 70%, up 4 points on last quarter

  - Best month was the last one, thanks to seasonality

### Sales pipeline
- Weighted pipeline of €1.75m for Q1 2027, with 9 deals in contract negotiation
  - Largest opportunity: Lowland Telecom at ~€91k; champion is Yasmin Zieliński (Senior Account Executive)

  - Data-protection questionnaires add two to three weeks on larger deals
- Inbound now about 52% of new pipeline
  - Founder posts and talks still drive most of it
  - Cold outbound works best with care-provider COOs
- Competition: seeing a lot more of insurers building their own apps
  - They win when time to value matters; they lose on breadth of features
  - Lost three deals last quarter to a bundled offer
- Sales team: 5 AEs ramped, founders still doing most discovery calls
  - Attainment around 58% across the team
  - First sales manager started in October
- Average deal size up to €60k as they move upmarket
  - Bigger deals come with longer pilots
- Self-serve trials at 198 a month, 14% convert to paid
  - Time to first value is the main lever for smaller teams

### Team

  - Attrition low in the last six months

- Fleur van Aken (VP Sales, Pallet Atlas)
- {{user:i01}} (General Partner, Stroopwafel Ventures)
- {{user:p09}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Monthly check-in with Iris Veldhuis and Fleur van Aken. We covered where the numbers are, go-to-market and market.

### Where the numbers are
- Run-rate revenue now at €6.21m, up 9% quarter on quarter
  - 52 new logos in the quarter; largest new contract €28k ACV
  - About 4% behind the board plan of €6.49m; one large renewal was delayed
- Net burn at €597k/month, runway until August 2028 (22 months)
  - Gross margin at 77%, flat on last quarter
  - The plan keeps the burn multiple under 1.8x
- Monthly revenue growth ran at 3% over the quarter
  - Strongest month was the last one, helped by a pricing change
- Cash in the bank at €13.1m after the last tranche
  - Collections slightly slower; DSO around 46 days
  - Treasury moved to a higher-yield account at the house bank
- 17,888 weekly active users across 688 customers
  - Daily-to-weekly ratio now 49%, the best engagement number so far
- Net revenue retention at 113%
  - Expansion driven by new departments adopting the product
  - 8 customers churned: a customer consolidating vendors after an acquisition
- 688 paying customers at an average contract value of €9k
  - Top 10 customers are 41% of revenue, down from 63% a year ago

### Go-to-market
- Deals with large consultancies keep stalling at security review
  - Happened twice this quarter, most recently with Ashgrove Strategy Partners
  - Iris thinks they are missing an internal sponsor
- Weighted pipeline of €2.6m for Q1 2027, and 3 deals in the final stages
  - Biggest opportunity: Havenlink Logistics at ~€56k; champion is Marloes Veldhuis (Head of Operations)
  - Win rate 25% over the last two quarters
- Sales cycle averaging 55 days
  - Procurement and legal add two to three weeks on larger deals
- Inbound now about 26% of new pipeline
  - An industry newsletter they sponsor drives a surprising share
  - Outbound works best with operations directors
- Competition: mostly up against two seed-stage copycats
  - They win when time to value matters; they lose on breadth of features
  - Dropped two deals last quarter on price alone
- Sales team: 9 AEs ramped and 2 SDRs
  - Attainment around 72% for ramped reps
  - New sales manager started in October

### Market
- Two seed-stage copycats announced a European launch this summer
  - No impact yet on win rates, though it shows up in more deals
- Win-loss review of the last 18 deals: the majority of losses against legacy on-premise vendors
  - Reason given: feature breadth
- Positioning reworked around time to value
  - New deck copy live in November
- Lock-in stronger than expected: three customers returned after trying a competitor
  - Retraining staff cited as the main reason
- Analyst coverage beginning to include the category
  - Could be worth a briefing in Q1 2027

### Expansion
- The Nordics is the priority market, a country lead planned for Q1 2027
  - 6% of pipeline already comes from the Nordics
  - Localisation in progress
- The UK parked until the Nordics proves out
  - Inbound from there served from Amsterdam for now
- Considering whether to hire a local team straight away
  - Iris prefers partners; {{user:i01}} pushed back
- Customer support in the local language required from day one
  - Plan: start with a part-time contractor

### Product & roadmap
- Shipped a mobile app for frontline users
  - Adoption at 50% of active customers after 6 weeks
  - Feedback mostly positive; main request is German and French localisation
- Released the integrations marketplace ahead of schedule
  - Took 4 weeks with four engineers
- Next up: an enterprise tier
  - Targeting end of Q1 2027
  - Noor thinks the date is realistic if scope stays fixed
- Spending ~30% of engineering time on platform work
  - Customer-facing incidents down from 7 to 1 per month
  - Noor wants to bring it down once the platform work lands
- Exploring AI assistance for first-line support questions
  - Plan is to include it for free until usage is proven
  - Early users report saving 2 hours a week
- Customer advisory board met last month with five customers
  - Top request: role-based permissions
  - Validated the next two roadmap items

### Board & reporting
- Next board meeting on 5 Nov
  - Agenda: the hiring plan and the pipeline review
  - Iris will circulate the pack a week ahead
- Discussed adding an independent board member with a finance background
  - A long-list of three to five names is due by the next meeting
- Board pack quality improving; request to add cohort retention to the KPI page
  - And a short summary up front so board members can skim
- ESOP grants for the last four hires to be approved at the next meeting
  - Pool has enough room for the hiring plan
- Plan for 2027 assumes 129% revenue growth and a flat burn
  - Board will probably push for a slower hiring plan

### Asks & opportunities
- Any intros to IT managers in the US as potential design partners.
- Implied: they lack a relationship with decision makers at consultancies like Ashgrove Strategy Partners; someone who knows how they buy would help.
- Referrals for the Solutions Engineer role (based in Rotterdam).
- Opportunity: Pallet Atlas could host a portfolio session on fundraising.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:i01}}: ask around the portfolio for IT managers in the US (by next week)
- [ ] {{user:i01}}: check who knows the financial-services practice at Ashgrove Strategy Partners (by end of month)
- [ ] {{user:i01}}: share two or three profiles for the Solutions Engineer role (by 28 Oct)
- [ ] Iris: share the draft board deck (by 18 Oct)

title: Notes from the Polder Climate Builders meetup
summary: Follow-ups from the Polder Climate Builders meetup: Wouter Zwart, Lukas Brandt and Niels Vermeulen.
body:
### Attendees
- Wouter Zwart (Senior Product Manager, Lanternfish)
- Lukas Brandt (Senior Data Scientist, Lumeno Scooters)
- Niels Vermeulen (Head of Partnerships, Lumacart)
- {{user:p17}} (Stroopwafel Ventures)

### Context
Conversations at the Polder Climate Builders meetup in Utrecht. Brief notes on the people worth following up with.

### Who we spoke with
- Wouter Zwart: Senior Product Manager at Lanternfish
  - Previously Associate Product Manager at Yondermere Health
  - Focused on roadmapping and product-led growth; interested in their next hire
- What Wouter needs: a sounding board on hiring
  - Low effort for us; good relationship builder
- Lukas Brandt: Senior Data Scientist at Lumeno Scooters
  - Previously Data Analyst at Tidewater Analytics
  - Working on forecasting and analytics; looking for their next hire
- How we could help: visibility for their programme
  - Easy win for us; good relationship builder
- Niels Vermeulen: Head of Partnerships at Lumacart
  - Previously Senior Partner Manager at Vitalis Diagnostics
  - Focused on partnerships and alliances; looking for startups in this space
- How we could help: visibility for their programme
  - Low effort for us; good relationship builder
- All in all, a good evening for portfolio support
  - Most three open to follow-up intros
- Follow-up with Wouter: an intro email this week
  - Context: shared interest in two of our companies in this area
- Next with Lukas: an invite to the next community evening
  - Why: overlap with two of our companies on this topic
- Follow-up with Niels: an intro email this week
  - Context: shared interest in our portfolio in this area

### Possible connections
- Niels could be useful for Tokenmill
  - Worth an intro after the event
- Niels could be useful for Annotaire (expert data labelling)
  - Worth a coffee once they're back from holiday
- More broadly, useful contacts for the operator network
  - {{user:p17}} to invite them to the next founder breakfast
- Could invite Wouter and Lukas and Niels to the next community evening
  - Would fit well in the founder crowd
- Plus a possible candidate for a portfolio company down the line
  - Will mention to the talent team for now

### Other notes
- Also chatted briefly with Florian Zimmermann (Head of Operations, Tellerbird)
  - Quick catch-up, no follow-up needed
- Event itself good mix of founders and corporates; worth going again
  - Good turnout from portfolio founders
- Format note: more time for networking would help next time
  - Will pass on the suggestion to the organisers
- Several Stroopwafel founders were there; good to see them in person
  - Two flagged fundraising timing to pick up in the next check-in
- Picked up a rumour that a large corporate is building a startup programme
  - Should check before our next call with them

### Key conversations
- Wouter Zwart (Senior Product Manager, Lanternfish) is focused on roadmapping and product-led growth
  - Interesting point: most teams underestimate onboarding
- Lukas Brandt (Senior Data Scientist, Lumeno Scooters) is focused on forecasting and analytics
  - Interesting point: procurement is the new bottleneck
- Niels Vermeulen (Head of Partnerships, Lumacart) is working on partnerships and alliances
  - Interesting point: hiring senior people is easier than a year ago
- General mood: busy, lots of hiring talk
  - Turnout around 188 people, more corporates than usual
- Plenty of founders asking about hiring senior engineers
  - Useful signal for the community programme
- Brought up a time they disagreed with their CEO
  - Dealt with it constructively, with data
- Best exchange of the evening was about hiring in a tight market
  - A few founders shared notes candidly
  - Worth sharing for the community

### Trends
- Lots of people mentioned procurement cycles getting longer
  - Matches what we hear in portfolio check-ins
- Corporates in the room mostly looking for AI use cases
  - A few wanted to know how to find relevant startups
- Investors there focused on vertical software over consumer
  - Plenty of interest in our view on grid software
- Talent market loosening for product managers
  - Salaries still rising year on year
- Lots of talk about the new EU rules for AI and what it means startups
  - Might make a good theme for a community event
- Less talk about crypto than last year; more about industrial AI
  - Reflects investor appetite right now

### Asks & opportunities
- Wouter would welcome intros to people working on roadmapping.
- Lukas would welcome intros to people working on forecasting.

### Next steps
- [ ] {{user:p17}}: send follow-up emails to everyone we met (by 16 Oct)
- [ ] {{user:p17}}: log the follow-ups in the CRM (by 23 Oct)
- [ ] {{user:p17}}: schedule the next check-in (by 21 Oct)
